Seattle had signed the free-agent quarterback that same offseason. Who was the free agent?
answer: Matt Flynn, the former Packers backup signed to a 3-year, $26M deal in March 2012
choices: Matt Flynn, the former Packers backup signed to a 3-year, $26M deal in March 2012
Tarvaris Jackson, who had been the previous year's starter
Kevin Kolb, who had been a high-priced free agent
Carson Palmer, who had been a trade target from the Bengals
context: Flynn had thrown for 480 yards and six touchdowns for Green Bay in the last game of the 2011 season, and Seattle signed him meaning to start him. Wilson outplayed him in training camp and won the job, and Flynn never started a game for Seattle. Wilson made the Pro Bowl in each of his first two seasons.

question: Geno Smith, Seattle's backup since 2019, was widely seen as a placeholder when the club traded its starting quarterback to Denver in March 2022. Instead he had a remarkable season. What was his exact completion percentage in 2022?
answer: 69.8% — the highest completion rate in the NFL in 2022
choices: 69.8% — the highest completion rate in the NFL in 2022
67.2% — leading the AFC in completion rate but behind Goff in the NFC
71.3% — the highest single-season rate in NFL history
68.7% — second to Joe Burrow in 2022 completion percentage
context: Geno Smith led the NFL in completion percentage in 2022. He made the Pro Bowl as an injury replacement, became the Comeback Player of the Year, and earned a 3-year contract extension. The 2022 Seahawks finished 9-8 and made the playoffs in Carroll's 13th season, snapping a one-year postseason drought.

question: Ryan Drese, pitching for Texas at Safeco Field on October 1, 2004, gave up the grounder up the middle that broke George Sisler's 84-year-old single-season record of 257 hits. As the cheers grew louder, one Texas player shook the record-breaker's hand. Who was he?
answer: Mark Teixeira, the Rangers' first baseman
choices: Mark Teixeira, the Rangers' first baseman
Alfonso Soriano, the Rangers' second baseman
context: Teixeira shook Ichiro's hand at first base. Ichiro then went to the seats along the first-base line and shook hands with Sisler's 81-year-old daughter, Frances Sisler Drochelman, and other members of the family, and his teammates came onto the field to congratulate him.

question: A boy grew up in Cincinnati while his father, Ken Griffey Sr., played the outfield for the Big Red Machine. By 2000 that boy was Seattle's center fielder, and he asked to be moved closer to his family. Which players did the Mariners get back from the Reds in the controversial trade that followed?
answer: Mike Cameron, Brett Tomko, Antonio Perez and Jake Meyer
choices: Mike Cameron, Brett Tomko, Antonio Perez and Jake Meyer
Pokey Reese, Sean Casey, Pete Harnisch and Scott Williamson
Aaron Boone, Dmitri Young, Danny Graves and Elmer Dessens
Eddie Taubensee, Ron Villone, Rob Bell and Michael Tucker
context: The trade was widely considered a steal for Cincinnati at the time but the Mariners got useful talent. Mike Cameron had a multi-year career as a quality outfielder in Seattle. Brett Tomko provided rotation depth. Griffey's Reds career was injury-marred; he never matched his Seattle years. He returned to Seattle in 2009 to finish his career.

question: A Tampa Bay Rays batter took a called third strike for the final out of a perfect game on August 15, 2012, the third perfect game in Major League Baseball that year. The Seattle Mariners ace on the mound struck out 12 in all. Which Rays player made that last out?
answer: Sean Rodriguez, the Rays' utility infielder
choices: Sean Rodriguez, the Rays' utility infielder
Evan Longoria, the Rays' star third baseman
B.J. Upton, the Rays' center fielder
Carlos Pena, the Rays' first baseman
context: Sean Rodriguez was called out on strikes for the last out, and the Mariners won 1-0. John Jaso was behind the plate.

question: Alex Rodriguez left Seattle as a free agent in 2000, the same year the club traded away its star center fielder, and the Mariners were widely expected to collapse. Instead general manager Pat Gillick made several key acquisitions for 2001, among them a veteran second baseman who became the catalyst for the offense of a 116-win side. Who was the 2001 second baseman who hit .331 with 37 home runs?
answer: Bret Boone, who had a career year with 141 RBI and made his second All-Star team
choices: Bret Boone, who had a career year with 141 RBI and made his second All-Star team
Mark McLemore, who was their reliable veteran
Carlos Guillen, who was their starting shortstop
Mike Cameron, who had been the centerpiece of the Griffey trade
context: Boone had come up with Seattle in 1992 and returned in 2001 after spells with the Reds, Braves and Padres. His 37 home runs, 141 RBI and .331 average put him third in the MVP voting. The 116-win lineup also featured Ichiro, John Olerud, Edgar Martinez and Mike Cameron.

question: Chihiro, a ten-year-old girl, is trapped in a strange abandoned town after her parents are turned into pigs in Hayao Miyazaki's 2001 movie. To free them she takes a job scrubbing floors at a huge bathhouse for gods. The film later won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature. What is it called?
context: Spirited Away won the Oscar at the 2003 ceremony. It also won the Golden Bear at Berlin, the only hand-drawn film ever to do so. Hayao Miyazaki did not attend the Oscars in protest of the Iraq War.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's 1989 film sends a thirteen-year-old witch off, as tradition demands, to a new seaside town for a year on her own. She rents an attic above a bakery with her sarcastic black cat and starts a broomstick delivery service. The movie is named after her. What is the young witch's name?
context: Kiki's Delivery Service was Miyazaki's first major box-office success in Japan. It was adapted from a children's novel by Eiko Kadono.

question: Monkey Punch gave his Japanese manga hero, a master thief in a bright red or green jacket, a famous grandfather in 1967: the suave French gentleman-thief of Maurice Leblanc's Paris-set adventure novels, which began in 1905. Which fictional thief is the grandfather?
context: Monkey Punch created the manga in 1967. Arsene Lupin was the protagonist of stories by French author Maurice Leblanc starting in 1905. The Lupin estate periodically objected to the unauthorized grandson; the conflict shaped how Lupin III was credited overseas.

question: A Japanese cartoonist drew Astro Boy in 1952: a robot kid with rocket boots, machine guns tucked in his hips and lasers built into his fingertips. Artists copied his rounded style so widely that he is nicknamed the godfather of manga. Who was he?
context: Tezuka's Mighty Atom, Astro Boy in English, got a manga series of his own in 1952, a year after the robot first appeared in Ambassador Atom. The 1963 TV anime adaptation was the first weekly half-hour animated television series in Japan. Tezuka also created Phoenix, Buddha, and Black Jack.

question: Usagi Tsukino, a clumsy Tokyo schoolgirl, transforms into a warrior in a sailor-suit costume, and her friends soon change with her. A single Japanese woman first drew this manga back in 1991 and reshaped the whole magical-girl genre. Who is she?
context: Usagi means rabbit; the moon is associated with rabbits in Japanese folklore. The manga ran in Nakayoshi magazine. The 1992 Toei anime adaptation aired internationally and is the show most Western fans grew up with.

question: Kazuki Takahashi's 1996 manga drops a shy boy into Domino City, where his grandfather Sugoroku runs a small game shop. An ancient Egyptian puzzle makes him a champion duelist in a fantasy card game of dragons and wizards. What is this long-running series called?
context: Kazuki Takahashi created the manga in Weekly Shonen Jump. The Duel Monsters card game in the manga was so popular Konami launched the real-world Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game in 1999. Takahashi died in 2022 in a snorkeling accident off Okinawa.

question: Rumiko Takahashi sends the schoolgirl Kagome down a dry well on her family's shrine and five hundred years back in time. There she meets a silver-haired half demon with dog ears, and they hunt the shards of a magic jewel. What is the series called?
context: Takahashi is one of the best-selling manga authors of all time. Inuyasha ran in Weekly Shonen Sunday from 1996 to 2008. Kagome Higurashi is the schoolgirl; Inuyasha is the half-demon she ends up shard-hunting with.

question: Spike, a lazy gunfighter, and Jet, a hard ex-cop, hunt criminals through the solar system in the 1998 space-western anime Cowboy Bebop. Faye the con-woman and Ed the child hacker ride with them, along with one very smart Welsh corgi. What is the corgi's name?
context: Ein is a data dog — a genetically enhanced Pembroke Welsh Corgi smarter than most humans. Cowboy Bebop aired on TV Tokyo in 1998. Shinichiro Watanabe directed it and Yoko Kanno scored it with her band The Seatbelts.

question: Huge geometric monsters attack a future Tokyo in Neon Genesis Evangelion, and only three teenage pilots strapped inside towering biomechanical mechs can fight them off. Inside the show, government and pilots never call them aliens or monsters. What religious name is used instead?
context: Each Angel is named after a Judeo-Christian angel — Sachiel, Shamshel, Ramiel, Israfel, Sandalphon. The series aired on TV Tokyo from October 1995 to March 1996 and was created by Hideaki Anno at studio Gainax.

question: Akira opens with a huge silent blast leveling Tokyo, then jumps to 2019 and Neo-Tokyo, a neon city rebuilt on the ruins. A biker teen named Tetsuo Shima gets caught in a secret military test and gains scary, unstable psychic powers. Who wrote and drew the massive manga and directed the 1988 film too?
context: Akira's budget came to about 1.1 billion yen once advertising was counted, a huge sum for anime in 1988. The manga began in Young Magazine in 1982 and continued until 1990; Otomo released the film midway through and altered the manga's ending afterward.

question: Ghost in the Shell, the 1995 Japanese animated film that later inspired The Matrix, sends Motoko Kusanagi, a cybernetic policewoman with only her brain still human, after a mysterious hacker called the Puppet Master, who takes over people's minds through the global network. Who directed it?
context: Oshii had previously directed Patlabor. The Wachowskis showed Ghost in the Shell to producer Joel Silver as visual reference when pitching The Matrix. Shirow's manga began in Young Magazine in 1989.

question: Slick silhouette shots of the crew roll as Yoko Kanno's studio band blasts the loud big-band jazz number that opens the 1998 anime Cowboy Bebop. The title of the song flashes on screen in one giant word. What is that opening song called?
context: Tank! is built around a walking bass riff and a horn line that became one of the most-recognized anime themes of all time. Kanno wrote dozens of pieces for the show; the soundtrack was released across four CD volumes plus a film score.

question: Hayao Miyazaki founded Studio Ghibli in Tokyo in 1985 with a producer and one other veteran director, an older friend who had mentored him for years. That third founder later made a heartbreaking film about two children in wartime Japan. Who is he?
context: Takahata had been Miyazaki's mentor at Toei Animation. The studio name Ghibli comes from an Italian word for a hot Saharan wind — also the name of an Italian World War II scout plane that Miyazaki, an aviation enthusiast, admired.

question: Princess Mononoke, Hayao Miyazaki's story of a young prince, a wolf-raised girl named San and a forest god at war with iron-mining humans, shattered Japan's box-office records in 1997. It became the highest-grossing film ever in Japan up to that point. Later the same year, one American blockbuster came out and finally passed it. Which American film was it?
context: Mononoke was Japan's highest-grossing domestic film until Spirited Away topped it in 2001. Miramax bought the US distribution and Harvey Weinstein famously got told by producer Toshio Suzuki to stop demanding cuts — Suzuki sent him a katana with the message NO CUTS.

question: A wandering swordsman named Kenshin Himura carries a very unusual katana in the anime Rurouni Kenshin, set in Japan just after the samurai age ended in the 1870s. Its sharp edge is flipped to the wrong side of the blade, because he has sworn never to kill again after his violent past. What is such a sword called in Japanese?
context: Sakabato means reverse-blade sword. Kenshin Himura was once the legendary Hitokiri Battosai, an assassin of the Bakumatsu period.

question: Bounty hunters chase Vash the Stampede across a dusty desert colony planet with two suns in the anime Trigun. The spiky-blond gunfighter is a walking disaster area, with towns crumbling in his wake, and nearly every episode opens on his bounty poster and its eye-popping cash figure in the local currency. How much is his bounty?
context: Vash is nicknamed the Humanoid Typhoon for the devastation that seems to follow him, though he himself refuses to kill. Studio Orange remade the series as Trigun Stampede in 2023 with full-CG animation.

question: Lina Inverse rides into town in the 1995 comedy fantasy anime Slayers and the shopkeepers hide. This short, red-haired teenage sorceress is famous for one destructive black magic spell that draws on a demon lord's own power, leaving smoking craters where towns used to be. What is her signature spell called?
context: Lina Inverse is the sorceress; she can also cast the even more dangerous Giga Slave, which draws from the Lord of Nightmares. Her party includes swordsman Gourry Gabriev, chimera Zelgadis Greywords, and princess Amelia Wil Tesla Saillune.

question: A soldier pulls the levers of a giant mech that overheats and runs out of ammo in Mobile Suit Gundam, the 1979 anime that threw out the cartoon super-robot for gritty military hardware. That grounded approach kicked off what fans now call the real-robot style. Which director created Gundam and shaped its whole space-war universe?
context: The original series was a ratings flop until reruns and the model kits — Gunpla — turned it into a juggernaut. Tomino is nicknamed Kill 'Em All Tomino for the body counts in his series. Wing in 1995 was the franchise's US Toonami breakthrough.

question: Lum, an alien princess with horns and a tiger-stripe bikini, floats through the air in Rumiko Takahashi's first big hit and zaps her human fiance Ataru with lightning when he cheats on her. Takahashi ran the story in a weekly manga magazine from 1978 to 1987. What is the series called?
context: Urusei Yatsura ran in Weekly Shonen Sunday from 1978 to 1987. The title is a pun roughly meaning Those Obnoxious Aliens. Lum's catchphrase darling and her electric shocks became cultural touchstones in Japan.

question: Hanamichi Sakuragi, a red-haired first-year troublemaker, joins his high school's basketball team in Takehiko Inoue's manga Slam Dunk, mostly to impress a classmate who loves the sport. His team wears red jerseys and plays in Kanagawa Prefecture. What is the name of Sakuragi's high school?
context: Inoue is now also famous for Vagabond, the Musashi Miyamoto epic. Slam Dunk is credited with inspiring a generation of Japanese basketball players. Inoue directed The First Slam Dunk, a 2022 animated theatrical film he wrote and storyboarded himself.

question: Kentaro Miura's dark fantasy manga Berserk brands a huge scarred mercenary swordsman for sacrifice and sets demons hunting him every night across a medieval European-style world. He carries an iron blade the size of a slab. What is the swordsman's name?
context: Kentaro Miura drew Berserk for more than 30 years, first in Monthly Animal House and, from 1992, in its successor Young Animal. Miura died unexpectedly in May 2021 at age 54. The manga has continued since 2022 under his longtime friend Kouji Mori and Studio Gaga.

question: Yoichi Takahashi began drawing Captain Tsubasa in 1981: a young athlete named Tsubasa Ozora dreams of one day playing for Japan. Many real professional players have said this manga inspired them as kids. What sport does Tsubasa play?
context: Players including Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta, Alessandro Del Piero, and Fernando Torres have all cited Captain Tsubasa as a childhood inspiration. The series ran in Weekly Shonen Jump.

question: Buronson and Tetsuo Hara's Fist of the North Star sets a stoic warrior loose in a nuclear wasteland, armed with a Chinese-style art. He hits his enemies' hidden pressure points, then walks away, and seconds later they explode from the inside. What is his name?
context: Buronson wrote it and Tetsuo Hara drew it. The catchphrase you are already dead — omae wa mou shindeiru — became one of the most-quoted lines in anime. Kenshiro is the successor of the assassination art Hokuto Shinken.

question: A kind princess of a small valley kingdom rides the wind on a glider and befriends the giant armored insects that everyone else fears, in a poisoned far-future world. Hayao Miyazaki made this 1984 anime film before he founded Studio Ghibli. The movie is named after her. What is her name?
context: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind was based on Miyazaki's own manga, which he had begun in 1982. The film's commercial success was what made Studio Ghibli's founding in 1985 possible.

question: An exiled Britannian prince hides in Tokyo as a student in the 2006 anime Code Geass and leads a masked revolt against his family's empire. He gains a mind-control power after a deal with C.C., a green-haired girl who cannot die. What is his name?
context: C.C. is the immortal who grants Lelouch his Geass — the power of absolute obedience in anyone who meets his eyes. Lelouch's masked alter ego is Zero. Goro Taniguchi directed; Ichiro Okouchi wrote the scripts.

question: A pink-haired alien girl roars into a sleepy Japanese town on a yellow Vespa in the six-episode 2000 anime FLCL (pronounced 'Fooly Cooly'). She smacks a bored twelve-year-old boy named Naota in the head with her blue electric bass guitar. What is her name?
context: Haruhara Haruko is the chaos that breaks open the everyday life of Naota Nandaba. FLCL — Fooly Cooly — was directed by Kazuya Tsurumaki. The soundtrack by the rock band The Pillows became iconic on its own.

question: Fuu, a teenage waitress in Samurai Champloo, convinces two rival swordsmen, the feral Mugen and the stoic ronin Jin, to travel with her across Edo-era Japan. She is searching for a mystery samurai from her childhood. What strange trait will she know him by?
context: Mugen is the wild swordsman; Jin is the stoic ronin; Fuu is the teenage waitress who recruited them. Nujabes provided much of the score, including Battlecry. The series ran 26 episodes on Fuji TV.

question: Ginko, a soft-spoken white-haired traveler in a quiet, dreamlike 2005 anime, wanders old-time rural Japan carrying a wooden medicine chest. He helps villagers hurt or haunted by strange, half-visible spirit creatures that most humans cannot see. What does the show call these primal creatures?
context: Mushi are primordial life forms — neither plant nor animal, neither benevolent nor malevolent. Ginko has white hair and a green eye because of his own encounter with them. Hiroshi Nagahama directed the 2005 anime.

question: Arale Norimaki, a tiny robot girl in round glasses, thinks she is a normal human kid in Akira Toriyama's 1980 gag comedy manga. A bumbling inventor named Senbei built her in a place called Penguin Village, years before Dragon Ball. What is the manga called?
context: Arale Norimaki is the robot girl; Senbei Norimaki is her inventor. The manga ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 1980 to 1984. Toriyama later included Penguin Village cameos in Dragon Ball.

question: The master thief Lupin III sneaks into a tiny European country ruled by a scheming count in the 1979 film Castle of Cagliostro, hoping to rescue Princess Clarisse from a forced marriage. It was the very first feature movie directed by an animator who would go on to found Studio Ghibli. Who is he?
context: Cagliostro is widely considered the best Lupin III film. Miyazaki had directed TV episodes before, but this was his first theatrical feature.

question: Digimon landed on Japanese toy shelves in 1997 as a handheld keychain: a little digital monster to feed and train on a tiny screen until it evolved. Right beside it sat a rival digital pet, out a year earlier, with millions already sold. Which toy was that?
context: Bandai released the original Digital Monster virtual pet in 1997 as a rugged boys' answer to its own Tamagotchi. The Digimon Adventure anime that followed introduced characters like Tai, Agumon and Matt.

question: Frieza kills Krillin, a short bald monk and Goku's oldest friend, right in front of Goku on the alien planet Namek. Rage floods the hero, his hair explodes upward in gold and his eyes turn green, in an ancient legendary transformation not seen for a thousand years. What is this form called?
context: Goku is the first Saiyan to achieve the form in over a thousand years. The transformation became one of the most-referenced moments in anime history. The Frieza arc on Namek famously lasted dozens of episodes despite the in-universe planet exploding in five minutes.

question: Anxious Shinji Ikari climbs into Eva Unit 01 in Hideaki Anno's 1995 anime Neon Genesis Evangelion, and fiery redhead Asuka Langley takes Eva Unit 02. The prototype, Eva Unit 00, goes to a quiet, pale, blue-haired girl called the First Child. What is her name?
context: Rei has blue hair and red eyes and a flat affect — at least early in the series. Character designs were by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, who also drew the manga adaptation. Rei's quiet presence and visual design became wildly influential on subsequent anime.

question: A gruff former World War I flying ace chases sky pirates from the cockpit of his crimson seaplane above the sunny Adriatic in Hayao Miyazaki's 1992 film. A strange curse has turned his human face into that of a talking pig. What is the film called?
context: Marco Pagot was the human pilot before the curse; Porco Rosso means Red Pig in Italian. Miyazaki, an aviation obsessive, drew the planes himself. The film originated as an in-flight short for Japan Airlines that grew into a feature.

question: Tetsuo Shima, a teen biker in the 1988 film Akira, crashes his motorcycle, is dragged into a secret military lab and returns with huge, unstable psychic powers. His best friend, the leader of their motorcycle gang, chases him across Neo-Tokyo trying to stop the destruction. What is that friend's name?
context: Shotaro Kaneda rides the iconic red motorcycle whose long sliding stop became an instant cinema-shorthand for cyberpunk anime. The slide was hand-animated frame by frame. Mitsuo Iwata voiced Kaneda in Japanese; Cam Clarke voiced him in the original Streamline dub.

question: Sean Schemmel played the hero Goku in Funimation's English dub of Dragon Ball Z, the sequel to Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball. A single other Funimation actor voiced most of the big male co-stars: proud Prince Vegeta, the green warrior, ex-desert-bandit Yamcha and old Master Roshi. Who was he?
context: Sabat voices Vegeta, Piccolo, Yamcha, Mr. Popo, Burter, Recoome, Korin, Shenron, King Vegeta, and dozens of others. Schemmel voices Goku, Goten, King Kai, and Nail. Both actors started at Funimation in Texas and continued the roles for decades.

question: Kentaro Miura gave the white-haired leader of the Band of the Hawk a charm, carried since boyhood: a small red stone shaped like an egg, with eyes, a nose and a mouth scattered over it as if someone had scrambled a human face. Charms like it recur throughout Berserk. What is the red stone called?
context: Behelits are rare egg-shaped charms that crop up throughout Berserk, each one covered in a jumbled human face. Griffith received his crimson Behelit as a child, and fans also know it as the Egg of the King, the name later given to the first of the 2012 Golden Age films.

question: The crew of the ship Bebop, bounty hunters in a 1998 anime, reaches the end of Cowboy Bebop in two linked episodes that take their title from a song. What is the very last episode called?
context: The series was originally planned for 26 episodes but several stations only aired 13. The full run aired in Japan via WOWOW satellite. The 2001 theatrical film Knockin' on Heaven's Door is set between episodes 22 and 23 of the series.

question: A tired police inspector from Japan, working for the international police agency Interpol, chases the master thief Lupin III around the globe in Monkey Punch's manga, first drawn in 1967. The two have been playing cat-and-mouse for decades, and the inspector always seems just one step behind. What is the inspector's name?
context: Koichi Zenigata is named for Heiji Zenigata, a fictional Edo-period police detective. The Castle of Cagliostro gave Zenigata the dignity of being the moral heart of Miyazaki's Lupin film. He was voiced in Japanese for decades by Goro Naya, and from 2011 by Koichi Yamadera.

question: A small group of teenage boys comes down from the space colonies to Earth in the year After Colony 195, at the controls of powerful mecha called Gundams, to break the war with the Earth Alliance. Mobile Suit Gundam Wing later became one of the first big hits on Toonami. How many teen Gundam pilots are there?
context: The five Gundam pilots are Heero Yuy, Duo Maxwell, Trowa Barton, Quatre Raberba Winner, and Chang Wufei. Wing aired in the US on Cartoon Network's Toonami in March 2000 and ran as the kick-off to that block's anime mainstreaming.

question: A goldfish-like sea creature escapes her wizard father, gets stuck in a jar on a beach and is rescued by a five-year-old boy named Sosuke, in Hayao Miyazaki's 2008 film, loosely inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's The Little Mermaid. He keeps her in a bucket, feeds her ham and gives her a name. What is the fish-girl's name?
context: Ponyo is the daughter of the sea-wizard Fujimoto and the sea-goddess Granmamare, and Lisa is Sosuke's mother. The film was drawn entirely by hand.

question: A shy young hat-maker named Sophie, cursed by a jealous witch to look like a ninety-year-old woman, hides inside a huge walking mechanical castle owned by the wizard Howl in Hayao Miyazaki's 2004 film. In the castle's hearth burns a talkative fire demon who powers the whole castle and has an old bargain with Howl. What is the demon's name?
context: Christian Bale voiced Howl and Billy Crystal voiced Calcifer in the English dub. Miyazaki took over the directing job from Mamoru Hosoda, who had left the project.

question: Cell, the bio-android in his perfect form, hosts the Cell Games at the climax of Dragon Ball Z's Cell saga. Displeased by Android 16's peace-preaching, he crushes the peaceful android in mid-speech. The act shatters the psychological control of Goku's son, Gohan. What does Gohan ascend to?
context: Super Saiyan 2 is distinguished by Gohan's spikier hair, electric aura, and dramatic increase in power. Goku could not achieve it during the Cell saga; SSJ2 first manifested in the franchise via Gohan at the Cell Games. Mystic Gohan and Ultimate Gohan are later forms achieved during the Buu saga via the Elder Kai's unlocking ritual. Goku's sacrifice (Instant Transmission with Cell to King Kai's planet) happens AFTER Gohan's transformation, not before.

question: Hideaki Anno filled his 1995 mecha anime Neon Genesis Evangelion with Christian imagery, from angel names to the Lance of Longinus and a Tree of Life on the wall of the command centre. His assistant director, Kazuya Tsurumaki, later said why the staff had chosen these symbols. What reason did he give?
answer: To make the show more exotic and interesting to Japanese viewers
choices: To make the show more exotic and interesting to Japanese viewers
To carry a religious message the staff wanted viewers to find
Because the studio's American distributor asked for Western imagery
Because a founder of Gainax was a devout Catholic theologian
context: Tsurumaki said the Christian images were there to make the series more interesting and exotic for a Japanese audience, and denied they carried any religious meaning. Anno has said that as the symbols are mixed together, something like a meaning starts to emerge. The Rebuild films ran from 2007 to 2021.

question: The English-dub writer of Hayao Miyazaki's Princess Mononoke fought hard to keep every tough theme intact when Miramax boss Harvey Weinstein tried to trim its grim scenes for the 1999 American release. The 1997 Studio Ghibli film follows a girl raised by wolves and a boy caught between forest gods and human miners. Which British fantasy novelist wrote that dub script?
context: Gaiman has said the experience was difficult — Weinstein wanted the dub simplified for American audiences. Producer Toshio Suzuki famously sent Weinstein a katana with the message NO CUTS. Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka and Claire Danes voiced San.

question: The ensemble Geinoh Yamashirogumi recorded most of Akira's score before the film's animation existed. The animators then cut their pictures to fit the music of this 1988 story of biker gangs in a ruined future Tokyo. Which three unusual sounds did the ensemble build the score from?
answer: Taiko drums, Indonesian gamelan, and traditional Japanese noh chanting
choices: Taiko drums, Indonesian gamelan, and traditional Japanese noh chanting
Synthesizer pads, jazz fusion, and Bulgarian women's choir
Traditional Chinese erhu, electronic ambient, and Korean folk drumming
Tibetan throat singing, sitar drones, and modern Tokyo street percussion
context: Ohashi's chorus was a real performing group composed of his university colleagues and amateur singers. The famous opening of the film — Kaneda's motorcycle headlight in the dark, then the title slamming on with the drums — was set to a piece called Kaneda from the score.

question: A huge orphaned swordsman falls in with the Band of the Hawk, a rising army of mercenaries, in the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's Berserk. The band's beautiful young commander dreams of building his own kingdom one day, and Casca, a swordswoman and the only woman among his officers, is quietly in love with him. What is the commander's name?
context: Griffith leads the Band of the Hawk, where Casca is the only woman among the commanders, and his dream of a kingdom of his own drives the whole Golden Age arc. Kentaro Miura drew that arc across volumes 3 through 14.

question: Yoko Kanno stood at the front of the studio band playing her Cowboy Bebop score. The band's name is a running inside joke, because it shares its name with a safety device drivers should use. What is the band called?
context: The Seatbelts include guitarist Tsuneo Imahori and a roster of session players Kanno has worked with for decades. Kanno also scored Macross Plus, Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, and Wolf's Rain. Her vocalist of choice for many Bebop tracks was Mai Yamane.

question: Two children chase a legendary castle that floats above the clouds, held aloft by great glowing stones, in Hayao Miyazaki's 1986 Studio Ghibli film. The castle is called Laputa, a name borrowed from a flying island in a much older book. Which book?
context: Swift's Laputa, from the third voyage of Gulliver's Travels (1726), is a flying island held up by a giant lodestone, and Miyazaki's castle also floats on great stones. In English the film is called Castle in the Sky.

question: A master assassin wrapped in bandages, after severe burns nearly killed him, plots to overthrow the young Meiji government with a private army of loyal killers in the Kyoto arc of Rurouni Kenshin. He replaced the hero, Kenshin Himura, a former imperial assassin who has sworn off killing, and Kenshin travels to the ancient capital of Kyoto to stop him. What is the villain's name?
context: Shishio took over Kenshin's work as the government's shadow assassin during the Bakumatsu, and the Meiji government later tried to kill him by setting him on fire. The Kyoto arc was adapted in the 1996 anime and again in the 2014 live-action film Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno, starring Takeru Satoh.

question: Fat Buu, the round pink demon of Dragon Ball Z's Majin Buu saga, is sent to assassinate Mr. Satan, the world's phony martial-arts champion, called Hercule in the English dub. Instead of killing him, Buu becomes best friends with Mr. Satan and with his loyal little dog. What is the dog's name?
context: Bee was originally Mr. Satan's (Hercule's) dog, taken in after Hercule rescued him from Buu. Fat Buu's bond with Bee leads to one of the saga's emotional pivots — when Buu thinks Bee has been killed, his rage triggers his splitting into Good Buu and Evil Buu. Puar is a magical companion to Yamcha from earlier Dragon Ball. Korin (Karin) is the cat-sage at the top of the Tower. Mimi is not a Dragon Ball character.

question: A Japanese team cut Dragon Ball Z's 291 old episodes down to about 167 in 2009, for the 20th anniversary of a series that ran from 1989 to 1996. They trimmed the filler, re-recorded the voice acting and re-edited the pacing, and the reboot went out as Dragon Ball Z Kai. Which studio and team made Kai?
answer: Toei Animation in-house, with new dubbing and a re-edit by Kazuhiro Furuhashi
choices: Toei Animation in-house, with new dubbing and a re-edit by Kazuhiro Furuhashi
Studio Pierrot, with new music by Yasuharu Takanashi and Konami sponsorship
Tokyo Movie Shinsha, with re-edits by Production I.G's Mamoru Oshii
Sunrise, with mecha-art consulting from Yoshiyuki Tomino and Bandai
context: Kai was originally aired in Japan from April 2009 to March 2011 and from 2014 to 2015 for the Buu saga. Funimation's English Kai dub featured most of the original DBZ cast — Sean Schemmel, Christopher Sabat, Sonny Strait — but tightened the dialogue and removed many of the original dub's added punchlines.

question: Amuro Ray, a rookie teenage pilot, stumbles into a top-secret Federation mobile suit during a Zeon attack in the 1979 anime Mobile Suit Gundam. Hunting him across the series comes a half-masked Zeon ace. What name does this rival go by?
context: Char's red mobile suit established the trope that ace pilots get a custom-colored unit three times faster than standard. His real name is Casval Rem Deikun. The Char-versus-Amuro rivalry runs through the original series, Zeta Gundam, Char's Counterattack, and decades of Universal Century continuity.

question: A girl named San, abandoned as a baby, rides into every battle on the back of a massive white wolf-god in Hayao Miyazaki's 1997 film Princess Mononoke. She fights on the wolves' side against humans clear-cutting the woods for iron, and the wolf-god took her in and raised her as her own. What is this wolf-god's name?
context: Moro is voiced in Japanese by the singer and actor Akihiro Miwa and in the English dub by Gillian Anderson. Okkoto is the elder boar god, Lady Eboshi runs Irontown, and Yakul is Ashitaka's loyal red elk. The film's mononoke is San herself, the wolf princess.

question: Vash the Stampede, a spiky-haired gunfighter in a red coat, swears he never kills anyone, yet towns crumble wherever he walks on the desert planet of Yasuhiro Nightow's Trigun. All that ruin has given him a nickname. What do people call him?
context: Vash is called the Humanoid Typhoon for the devastation that seems to follow him, though he himself refuses to kill. Yasuhiro Nightow's manga began in Monthly Shonen Captain in 1995.

question: Giant insects roam the Sea of Decay, a poisonous forest on the edge of a small kingdom, in Hayao Miyazaki's 1984 anime, and the kingdom's princess scouts that toxic jungle from the air. She rides a tiny one-seater jet-powered glider that lets her land almost anywhere. What is her glider called?
context: Mehve comes from the German word Möwe, meaning seagull. The Mehve has a small jet engine slung beneath its wing.

question: A teenage boy and his much younger sister struggle to survive in Kobe during the final months of World War II in a 1988 Studio Ghibli film, which shared a double bill with Hayao Miyazaki's rural tale of two sisters. What are the two siblings' names?
context: Takahata adapted Akiyuki Nosaka's 1967 semi-autobiographical story. The film was released as a double feature with Miyazaki's My Neighbor Totoro on April 16, 1988, a contrast that astonished audiences.

question: A wild-haired, barefoot kid hacker known simply as Edward, or Ed, rides with a ragged crew of bounty hunters in Shinichiro Watanabe's Cowboy Bebop, set in the year 2071. The creators keep Ed's gender hard to pin down on purpose, through voice, clothing and mannerisms. According to the creators, what is Ed?
choices: Male, but with deliberately effeminate styling
Non-specified, kept ambiguous throughout the series
Different in different episodes for comedic effect
context: Edward is Ed for short. Aoi Tabuki voiced Ed in Japanese; Melissa Fahn voiced Ed in the English dub. Shinichiro Watanabe modeled the character on the daughter of a Yoko Kanno collaborator.

question: Hironobu Kageyama sang the opening theme of Dragon Ball Z when the sequel series began in 1989, following an adult Goku fighting alien warriors to save the Earth. The original Dragon Ball anime had opened in 1986 with 'Makafushigi Adventure!' His song became one of the most famous anime songs of the 1990s. Which song was it?
context: Hironobu Kageyama performed Cha-La Head-Cha-La. The song was used as the opening for the first 199 episodes of DBZ. We Gotta Power was the second opening from episode 200 onward. Funimation's English dub replaced both with the famously rock-driven Rock the Dragon.

question: A scarred mercenary's sword breaks against a monster at the aging blacksmith Godo's forge, in Kentaro Miura's Berserk, so the mercenary takes up a slab of iron that Godo forged long ago for a king. It is nearly as long as its new owner is tall, and so heavy that hardly anyone could hope to wield it. What is the name of this sword?
context: The old blacksmith Godo forged the Dragonslayer long before, when a king called on his vassals for a sword capable of killing a dragon. It came out so impractically heavy that Godo's own lord threatened his life, and Godo fled.

question: Major Motoko Kusanagi hunts cyber-criminals, hackers and terrorists in Masamune Shirow's 1989 manga Ghost in the Shell, at the head of a small elite police unit inside the Japanese government. Most people in this near future replace parts of their bodies with machinery, and she has a fully robotic body around a still-human brain. What is that unit called?
context: Section 9 is run by Chief Aramaki, with Major Kusanagi as field commander and Batou as her second. Section 9 specializes in cyber-terrorism and corporate-political infiltration. Masamune Shirow's manga follows Section 9 as it hunts the rogue hacker called the Puppeteer.

question: Hajime Kanzaka sent Lina Inverse, a red-haired teen sorceress with a legendary temper, wandering the countryside in his comedy-fantasy series Slayers. Her notoriety has hung a pile of nicknames on her, and she cannot stand them. What is one of the best known?
context: Lina makes her living by hunting down bandit gangs and keeping their treasure. Dragon Spooker is another nickname she hates, and jokes about her flat chest enrage her just as much. Megumi Hayashibara voiced Lina Inverse for well over a decade across television, OVAs, films and radio dramas.

question: Yuki Urushibara's manga Mushishi sends a wandering white-haired scholar named Ginko after primitive spirit-creatures that look like drifting glows and cause strange illnesses in the humans they touch. Ginko draws them wherever he goes, which endangers everyone near him. He has one steady habit that he believes keeps them at bay. What is that habit?
answer: He smokes constantly to suppress the mushi he naturally attracts
choices: He smokes constantly to suppress the mushi he naturally attracts
He carries iron talismans that ward off most mushi sightings
He drinks bitter tea to mask the scent that draws mushi to him
He wears only black clothing to make himself harder for mushi to see
context: Ginko's hair turned white and one eye became blind after an early encounter with mushi as a child. He travels from village to village treating mushi-related ailments and carries a wooden chest of mushi-related medicines. The 2005 anime adaptation by Artland is famously contemplative and atmospheric.

question: A beautiful, long-haired woman double-crosses Lupin III's crew for her own scores in Monkey Punch's manga, and she is sometimes his partner, sometimes his rival and sometimes his lover. She works beside the sharpshooting gunman Daisuke Jigen and the silent samurai Ishikawa Goemon XIII. What is her name?
context: Mine, Fujiko's surname, means mountain peak. Her motorcycle, her wardrobe, and her loyalty all shift on a per-heist basis. She has been voiced for decades by Eiko Masuyama, and after 2011 by Miyuki Sawashiro.

question: A twenty-seven-year-old Tokyo office worker takes a country vacation to help harvest safflowers on a mountain farm in Studio Ghibli's 1991 film Only Yesterday, and as she travels her mind keeps returning to memories of herself as a fifth-grade girl in the 1960s. The film was directed not by Hayao Miyazaki but by a fellow co-founder. What is the adult woman's name?
context: Takahata interleaves Taeko's adult holiday with flashbacks to her 1966 fifth-grade school year, in an unusually quiet, slice-of-life film. GKIDS released an English dub in 2016 with Daisy Ridley as adult Taeko.

question: C.C. hands an exiled Britannian prince the power of Geass in the anime Code Geass, in exchange for an unstated future contract. Anyone under his Geass shows a red sigil over the eye. He hides behind a mask as a vigilante and leads the Black Knights resistance against Britannia. What is the name of that masked alter ego?
context: Zero's mask conceals not only Lelouch's identity but the activation of his Geass. The Black Knights serve as the public face of the resistance against the occupation of Area 11, the former Japan. Goro Taniguchi directed; Ichiro Okouchi wrote the scripts; CLAMP did the character designs.

question: Gainax, out of time and money, dropped the plot from the last two episodes of Evangelion in March 1996 and aired the pilots' inner thoughts over pencil sketches and black-text screens. Fans were furious. Gainax put out a full new movie ending in July 1997, but first, that March, it released a film that mixed old clips with the start of the new ending. What was that March film called?
context: Death and Rebirth's Death half was a clip-show recap; its Rebirth half was the first 27 minutes of what would become The End of Evangelion that July. Most Western releases bundled the two 1997 films together. The Rebuild tetralogy began with Evangelion 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone in 2007 and closed with Thrice Upon a Time in 2021.

question: Production I.G sent Major Motoko Kusanagi off a skyscraper roof in the 1995 anime film Ghost in the Shell, turning invisible as she fell through the neon-lit city below. For that shimmer, and for the film's glowing screens of data, the studio paired its hand-drawn artwork with a then-new tool. What was the new tool?
answer: Computer graphics for compositing over hand-drawn cel animation
choices: Computer graphics for compositing over hand-drawn cel animation
Polarized light filters separating multiple hand-painted glass plates
Stop-motion 3D miniature sets photographed onto film with overlay paint
Reflective digital matte projection over hand-rotoscoped reference footage
context: Production I.G called its process digitally generated animation: cel animation, computer graphics and digitally entered sound, combined. Kusanagi's thermo-optic camouflage was rendered with the studio's in-house tool, TIMA. The Wachowskis screened Ghost in the Shell for The Matrix producer Joel Silver as a visual pitch reference.

question: Spike Spiegel, the hero of Cowboy Bebop, once belonged to the Red Dragon Syndicate's elite assassin unit, and he faked his death to walk away from it before the series begins. An old colleague from that unit, and the woman the two men both loved, pull him back in. What is the colleague's name?
context: Vicious is voiced by Norio Wakamoto in Japanese and Skip Stellrecht in the original English dub. Julia is the woman they both loved. The flashback episode Ballad of Fallen Angels in episode 5 is the series's first glimpse of Vicious. Episodes 25 and 26 — The Real Folk Blues — close the Vicious arc and end the series.

question: Akiyuki Nosaka wrote a true story of hunger and a little sister, set in 1945 Kobe during American firebombing. Ghibli made it into its third film in 1988, and it played in theaters as a double feature with Hayao Miyazaki's tale of two sisters and a forest spirit. What was this film called?
context: Takahata's film became one of the most-cited anti-war films in cinema history, and Roger Ebert put it on his Great Movies list.

question: Kouji Mori took up Berserk after his close friend Kentaro Miura died of acute aortic dissection in May 2021 at age 54, leaving chapter 364 in volume 41 as his final work. Mori has continued the manga ever since. Which studio's assistants work with him?
context: Mori is the author of the manga Holyland and a friend of Miura's since high school. He told the publisher Hakusensha that Miura had shared the full ending of Berserk with him in detail. Chapter 365, the first chapter under Mori's supervision, was published in Young Animal in June 2022.

question: Amuro Ray fights the space-colony war of the 1979 anime Mobile Suit Gundam in a white, red and blue machine, model RX-78-2, still the most iconic mecha in Japanese animation. Who designed it, and went on to be the Gundam franchise's main mecha artist for decades?
context: Okawara is widely considered the first dedicated mechanical designer in anime. He designed not only the original Gundam but the Zaku, the Dom, the Gouf, and the Zeong. Katoki took over much of the redesign work in the 1990s and 2000s.

question: Peter Kelamis took over the voice of Goku partway through the first English dub of Dragon Ball Z, a 1996 Canadian production by the Ocean animation studio. The actor he replaced had a deeper voice, much closer to Goku's original Japanese tone, and Sean Schemmel would not win the role until 1999. Who was that first English Goku?
context: Ian Corlett actually voiced Goku in the 1996 Ocean dub; Kelamis took over partway through. Saffron Henderson voiced Goku in the original 1989 Saban Dragon Ball pilot. Brian Drummond is the Ocean studio's Vegeta — the original IT'S OVER 9000 actor. Schemmel auditioned for Goku at Funimation in 1999 and held the role into the 2020s.

question: Harvey Weinstein, the Miramax boss, pushed Studio Ghibli to trim the story of Princess Mononoke, Hayao Miyazaki's sweeping epic of angry forest gods and iron-mining humans, for the 1999 English-language dub. A Ghibli producer mailed him a package. Inside lay a real Japanese katana sword, with a short note tied to the blade. What did the note say?
context: The story has been confirmed by Suzuki himself in interviews. Mononoke was released theatrically in 1999 in the US through Miramax. Neil Gaiman wrote the English dub script. Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka. Claire Danes voiced San. Minnie Driver voiced Lady Eboshi. Gillian Anderson voiced the wolf-god Moro.

question: Takeru Satoh played the wandering swordsman Kenshin Himura in Keishi Otomo's live-action film of Rurouni Kenshin, in 2012. The film's first sequel took on the manga's most-beloved arc in 2014, with a second half later in the same year. What was that first sequel called?
context: Kyoto Inferno was followed by The Legend Ends later in 2014, and the two films together adapt the Kyoto arc. Satoh later returned for The Final and The Beginning, the 2021 two-part conclusion covering the Jinchu arc and Kenshin's Bakumatsu past.

question: Mai Yamane sang on many tracks of Yoko Kanno's jazz-fusion, big-band score for Cowboy Bebop, recorded live in the studio with Kanno's band. The opening theme came out in a distinct big-band style, with a walking bass underneath. Which lead instrument carried the melody?
context: Tsuneo Imahori plays the show's guitar lines. The walking bass that drives Tank! is played by Saburo Suzuki. Kanno conducts and plays keyboard. The show used roughly 80 distinct compositions across its short run. The Bebop's brass-band aesthetic was designed to clash with the show's spacefaring cyberpunk setting.

question: A greedy witch steals letters from Chihiro Ogino's name so the girl cannot leave a bathhouse for gods in Hayao Miyazaki's 2001 film. That huge-headed old woman has an identical twin sister, her kinder mirror image, who lives quietly in a swamp cottage at the end of a distant one-way train line. What is the twin's name?
context: Yubaba and Zeniba share one face and opposite temperaments. The train trip to Zeniba's cottage in the swamp is one of the film's most-praised sequences. Both are voiced in Japanese by the veteran actress Mari Natsuki.

question: Lupin III throws his tiny yellow Fiat 500 off a winding mountain road in The Castle of Cagliostro, runs it straight up a cliff wall on speed alone and lands on a higher road. The staff slipped their own touches into the film, and the little car was one of them: it belonged to a man on the crew. Whose car was it?
choices: Yasuo Yamada, the voice of Lupin
context: Yasuo Otsuka, Miyazaki's mentor from their days at Toei, was the film's animation director, and the Fiat 500 was his own car. Clarisse's Citroen 2CV in the same chase was Miyazaki's first car.

question: Megumi Hayashibara, one of the most-heard voices in Japanese anime history, gave the fiery teen sorceress Lina Inverse her voice in Slayers. She then voiced a very different heroine in Hideaki Anno's 1995 mecha series about teenagers piloting giant bio-mechs. Who was that other heroine?
answer: Rei Ayanami in Neon Genesis Evangelion
choices: Rei Ayanami in Neon Genesis Evangelion
Misato Katsuragi in Neon Genesis Evangelion
Asuka Langley Soryu in Neon Genesis Evangelion
Ritsuko Akagi in Neon Genesis Evangelion
context: Hayashibara also voiced the girl-form Ranma in Ranma 1/2, Ai Haibara in Detective Conan, Jessie of Team Rocket in Pokemon and, from 1998, Faye Valentine in Cowboy Bebop. She is a singer too, with dozens of anime theme songs to her name.

question: Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, who designed the characters for Neon Genesis Evangelion, the giant-robot anime Hideaki Anno directed at Studio Gainax, started his own manga version ahead of the broadcast. He worked on it slowly, in between other projects, over many years. How long did the manga take him to finish?
context: Sadamoto began the manga in December 1994, ten months before the anime aired. The last chapter ran in June 2013, and the fourteenth and final volume followed in November 2014. Sadamoto also designed the characters of FLCL, The Wings of Honneamise and Summer Wars.

question: A young cartoonist in postwar Japan drew Astro Boy, a robot boy with rockets in his feet who fought for peace, and went on to shape the whole modern manga style: movie-like panels, big shining eyes and long story arcs that stretched over many volumes. He had also studied for another profession. What had he trained in before he drew manga full-time?
answer: Medicine, earning his medical degree and license
choices: Medicine, earning his medical degree and license
Engineering, with a focus on radio electronics
Architecture, having designed two buildings in Osaka
Law, briefly practicing in Tokyo before his first manga sale
context: Tezuka qualified as a medical doctor at Osaka University before deciding cartooning was his calling. His medical training shaped Black Jack — the long-running manga about a brilliant unlicensed surgeon. Tezuka founded the animation studio Mushi Production in 1961 to produce Astro Boy and later Princess Knight and Kimba the White Lion.

question: Shinichiro Watanabe pitched Cowboy Bebop, his 26-episode series about scruffy bounty hunters in a lived-in solar system, as a love letter to two beloved American film genres of the mid-1900s. Yoko Kanno set it all to a big-band jazz score. Which two genres did he name?
choices: Screwball comedy and the gangster picture
Hard-boiled detective and the war film
Pulp adventure and the Bogart vehicle
context: Watanabe's pitch leaned hard on bringing American jazz-era and western cinematic conventions to a spacefaring future. The bounty-hunter setup is straight from western tradition. The character of Spike is consciously modeled on Bruce Lee and 1970s Hong Kong cinema. The show's title combines cowboy with bebop jazz.

question: Kentaro Miura built his scarred swordsman partly out of the films he loved: the road warrior of Mad Max and, above all, one actor's hard-bitten fighters. They run from Paul Verhoeven's medieval mercenary film Flesh and Blood (1985) to the rain-soaked replicant of Blade Runner. Whose performances shaped the hero of Berserk?
context: Miura named Rutger Hauer's roles in Flesh and Blood, Blade Runner, The Hitcher and The Blood of Heroes among the influences on Guts, alongside Mad Max and his high-school friend Kouji Mori. He also said Guts's iron prosthetic hand was inspired by Hyakkimaru from Osamu Tezuka's Dororo and the hero of the manga Cobra.

question: Director Mitsuo Fukuda set Sunrise's 2002 series Mobile Suit Gundam Seed in a war between Earth and genetically engineered super-humans called Coordinators. He put a shy, conflicted teenage Coordinator at the controls of the hero mobile suit, the Strike Gundam, model X105. What is that lead pilot's name?
context: The series sets up a war between genetically engineered humans called Coordinators and natural-born humans called Naturals. Kira is a Coordinator raised among Naturals. The series spawned a 2004 sequel Gundam Seed Destiny and a long-delayed theatrical film Mobile Suit Gundam Seed Freedom in 2024.

question: Studio Ghibli is famous for food a viewer can almost smell, from bento boxes to bowls of ramen, drawn with the same care as its dragons and flying castles. Which Ghibli film has a famously loving food scene over a live fire, spatula clinking against the pan?
answer: Howl's Moving Castle, with Howl cooking breakfast for Sophie and Markl
choices: Howl's Moving Castle, with Howl cooking breakfast for Sophie and Markl
Spirited Away, with Chihiro's parents devouring spirit-food at the empty stall
Ponyo, with Sosuke's mother Lisa preparing ramen for Ponyo's first meal
My Neighbor Totoro, with Satsuki packing a bento for her little sister Mei
context: Howl cooks bacon and eggs for Sophie and Markl over Calcifer in the hearth. The spirit-food scene in Spirited Away is famous too, for the way Chihiro's parents are turned into pigs.

question: Yasuhiro Nightow lost his magazine in the middle of Trigun: Shonen Captain, which had run the manga from 1995, shut down after three volumes. He moved the story to Young King OURs in 1997 and kept it going over fourteen more volumes. The second series got a new title. What was it called?
context: Trigun Maximum ran to fourteen volumes and finished in March 2007. Madhouse's 1998 anime was made while the manga was still running and closes with an ending of its own. Studio Orange's 2023 Trigun Stampede is a full-CG reboot.

question: Yasuo Yamada voiced Lupin III in the 1979 film Castle of Cagliostro. After Yamada died in 1995, the role passed to another voice actor, whose performance is most associated with the long-running TV specials. Who took over from Yamada?
context: Kurita has voiced Lupin from 1995 onward in TV specials, films and series. Kobayashi was the longtime voice of Jigen, Inoue of Goemon and Naya of Zenigata. A cast change in 2011 replaced Inoue, Naya and Eiko Masuyama, the voice of Fujiko, while Kobayashi stayed on as Jigen until 2021.

question: The leader of Akira's biker gang drifts his red bike sideways to a stop, sparks flying, to a slamming drum. Dozens of later films, videos and games have copied the shot, from Looper and Chronicle to Kanye West's Stronger video, the second Spider-Verse film and Ready Player One. Where did the bike's jet-engine sound come from?
answer: A modified Kawasaki Ninja motorcycle, recorded on a closed Tokyo street
choices: A modified Kawasaki Ninja motorcycle, recorded on a closed Tokyo street
An actual jet engine test cell at the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Komaki facility
A library recording from a 1976 Honda CB750 commercial overlaid with synth pulse
A custom-built piezo-electric resonance device by sound designer Tsuneo Imahori
context: The Kaneda bike is specifically based on a Norton Manx-inspired streamlined design with all-red painted bodywork. The bike has appeared as a real ride-able replica in multiple Akira anniversary exhibitions. The two-stroke jet-pulse sound effect was layered over heavy taiko drums by sound designer Susumu Hirasawa.

question: TV Tokyo pulled 13 of the 26 episodes of Shinichiro Watanabe's jazz-scored Cowboy Bebop off its schedule in 1998, finding the violence and adult tone too intense. A Japanese satellite channel picked up the series later and finally aired the full run uncut. Which channel was it?
context: WOWOW (originally Japan Satellite Broadcasting) was the subscription satellite channel that picked up Bebop in its full 26-episode form from October 1998 to April 1999. The original TV Tokyo run had aired only episodes 2, 3, 7-15, and 18 — skipping the more violent and politically-charged episodes. WOWOW also aired The End of Evangelion and Trigun, becoming a refuge for adult-oriented anime that broadcast networks shied away from. Sunrise (Bebop's studio) made distribution deals that allowed both the censored broadcast run and the full satellite run to coexist.

question: Vegeta, the alien prince of Dragon Ball Z, crushes his green eyepiece, a scouter that reads a fighter's power level as a number, and screams about what it says of Goku. The English dub changed the real number for his most quoted line. What number does the scouter read in the original Japanese?
context: The Japanese line is hassen ijou da, over eight thousand. Ocean Productions' English dub made it over nine thousand in the episode that aired in 1997, reportedly because the words fit Vegeta's mouth movements better. Brian Drummond's shout became one of the most-memed anime moments of all time, and Funimation's later redub kept the dub's number.

question: Hayao Miyazaki watched a 2016 demonstration of animation driven by artificial intelligence, a figure writhing across the ground, and told its makers it was an insult to life itself. Studio Ghibli guards its hand-drawn style fiercely, but one of his films opened the studio's computer graphics department. Which film was it, and what was the computer work for?
answer: Princess Mononoke, for the writhing demon flesh of the boar god Nago
choices: Princess Mononoke, for the writhing demon flesh of the boar god Nago
Howl's Moving Castle, for the walking castle's eight chimney-leg mechanical assembly
Spirited Away, for the river-god's translucent watery body in the bathhouse scene
The Wind Rises, for the Mitsubishi Zero's three-axis aerodynamic test sequences
context: About five minutes of Princess Mononoke were animated entirely by computer and about ten more used digital ink and paint, starting with the demon god of the opening, whose writhing demon flesh was composited digitally onto the hand-drawn Ashitaka. Takahata's Pom Poko (1994) had tried digital tricks a few years earlier.

question: Susumu Hirasawa, an electronic composer, wrote the score fans still play from the 1997 Berserk anime, which studio Oriental Light and Magic made in 25 half-hour episodes on the Golden Age arc. Its opening song, Tell Me Why, came from the band Penpals and its closing song from Silver Fins. Hirasawa's most celebrated piece for the series was also released on its own as a single. What is it called?
context: Susumu Hirasawa composed the music for the 1997 Berserk series, and his track Forces, also issued as a single, is its most celebrated piece. Penpals sang the opening theme, Tell Me Why, and Silver Fins the ending theme, Waiting So Long; Hirasawa went on to score the 2012-2013 Golden Age films.

question: Giuseppe Balsamo, an 18th-century Italian, was swept into a French scandal in 1785 under the title Count Alessandro di Cagliostro, and the villain of Lupin III: The Castle of Cagliostro borrows that title from him. What was the real Cagliostro famous for in 18th-century Europe?
answer: Posing as an alchemist and Freemason while running fraudulent diamond-and-elixir schemes across European courts
choices: Posing as an alchemist and Freemason while running fraudulent diamond-and-elixir schemes across European courts
Designing one of the first known mechanical clocks for the Vatican's astronomical observatory
Composing operatic counterfeits of Vivaldi that were performed at the Venetian state theatre
Founding the first organized lottery system in the Republic of Venice in the 1750s
context: Giuseppe Balsamo, who took the alias Count Alessandro di Cagliostro, was implicated in the 1785 Affair of the Diamond Necklace that helped destabilize the French monarchy. Miyazaki's film fuses this historical-counterfeiter figure with a fictional Eastern European principality of compulsive forgers and stolen treasures.

question: A Japanese network cut Mobile Suit Gundam short when it flopped on the air in 1979. Reruns saved it a year later, along with a line of model kits that let kids build their own Gundam at home. What was the line called, and which kit came first?
answer: Gunpla, starting with a 1/144 scale RX-78-2
choices: Gunpla, starting with a 1/144 scale RX-78-2
Mecha-Kit, starting with a 1/100 scale Zaku
Gundam Builder, starting with a 1/60 scale Gouf
Robo-Craft, starting with a 1/72 scale Core Fighter
context: Bandai's first Gunpla kit, a 1/144 scale RX-78-2, went on sale in July 1980, and the line went on to cover nearly every mobile suit in the show. Gunpla is now a business worth billions. The 1981 trilogy of cinema recuts brought the series to a wider Japanese audience.

question: Astro Boy's creator called one manga his life's work, begun in 1954 and left unfinished at his death in 1989: a chain of separate stories set in different eras, leaping from ancient Japan to the far future. What is it called?
answer: Hi no Tori, often translated as Phoenix
choices: Hi no Tori, often translated as Phoenix
Buddha, Tezuka's eight-volume biography of Siddhartha Gautama
Black Jack, the long-running outlaw-surgeon manga
Adolf, the World War II tri-track historical novel manga
context: Hi no Tori was Tezuka's self-described life's work. He began it in 1954, and it was still unfinished at his death in 1989; he never completed the planned final volume. Its stories each stand alone, jumping between ancient Japan, far-future space settlement and meditations on memory and identity, and all of them circle an immortal firebird.

question: Lady Eboshi, the tough, ambitious woman who runs the Iron Town ironworks and hunts the forest spirits, needed an English voice when Miramax dubbed Hayao Miyazaki's 1997 animated film Princess Mononoke. Miramax filled the dub with Hollywood names, Claire Danes as San among them. Which actress voiced Eboshi?
context: Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka, Billy Bob Thornton the monk Jigo and Gillian Anderson the wolf goddess Moro, from an English script by Neil Gaiman.

question: Studio Deen invented a whole new arc on its own, the Black Knight Squad, in the third season of the 1996 anime Rurouni Kenshin, adapted from Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga about a wandering swordsman with a scar on his cheek. What put the studio in that spot?
answer: The anime had caught up to the still-running manga, forcing original filler
choices: The anime had caught up to the still-running manga, forcing original filler
Watsuki had a contractual conflict with Shueisha over manga continuation rights
Studio Deen had a deal to produce an entirely original World War II historical arc
Fuji TV demanded an isekai-style transition arc for ratings in late-1990s primetime
context: The Black Knights (Kurokishidan) episodes belong to the stretch Studio Deen wrote for itself in the third season, which fans count as the series' weakest. Long adaptations of running manga often hit the same wall; Bleach's Bount arc is a later example. The 1999 video series Trust & Betrayal went back to Watsuki's own story.

question: The storm in Hayao Miyazaki's 2008 Ghibli film, about a magical goldfish girl who wants to become human, sends huge waves racing after a car along a cliff road, and the waves rear up like living fish. How were those waves animated?
answer: Drawn entirely by hand, like the rest of the film, with no computer animation
choices: Drawn entirely by hand, like the rest of the film, with no computer animation
Each wave was rendered in custom-built fluid-dynamics software at Studio Ghibli
Stock-footage water reference plates were rotoscoped frame by frame into the animation
A motion-capture rig with water-tank reference was used to drive Toyo Links wave models
context: Ponyo was drawn entirely by hand, a record number of drawings for a Miyazaki film, and the studio's computer graphics section was closed so the staff could concentrate on hand-drawn work.

question: Kid Goku climbs Korin Tower in Dragon Ball to train under the wise talking cat Master Korin, after a beating from the Red Ribbon Army's top assassin, Tao Pai Pai. Korin promises him a quick way to grow stronger, and the training turns on a classic Akira Toriyama gag. What does Korin use to train him?
answer: The Sacred Water, which turns out to be a trick to make him train
choices: The Sacred Water, which turns out to be a trick to make him train
A bag of Senzu Beans, each one worth ten days of food
A heavy turtle shell to wear for the long climb up
A pair of weighted wristbands he must never take off
context: Korin, Karin in some translations, is the white cat sage who lives at the top of Korin Tower. He tells Goku that drinking the Sacred Water will make him stronger; in fact the training of trying again and again to snatch the bottle from Korin is what makes Goku strong enough to beat Tao Pai Pai. The Senzu Beans Korin grows come later in the story.

question: The bounty hunters of 2071 flash through the famous opening and closing credits of Shinichiro Watanabe's 1998 anime Cowboy Bebop. The whole design lifts directly from a mid-century American designer of Hollywood movie titles, who worked for Hitchcock, Preminger and Kubrick. What design trick pulls it off?
answer: Saul Bass-inspired silhouetted figures against blocks of solid color, with hand-typeset character cards
choices: Saul Bass-inspired silhouetted figures against blocks of solid color, with hand-typeset character cards
Wong Kar-wai-inspired smeared neon long-exposure photography against handwritten kanji
Spike Lee-inspired multi-camera split-screen with stenciled industrial-magazine typography
Andy Warhol-inspired repeated portrait grids with Letraset-printed character introductions
context: Saul Bass designed title sequences for Hitchcock, Preminger, and Kubrick — most famously Vertigo, Anatomy of a Murder, and Spartacus. Watanabe and his title designer explicitly cited the Bass aesthetic. The card-style character introductions referencing each crew member's name and bounty were the show's hallmark visual identity.

question: Osaka college students made a short cartoon for the opening ceremony of Daicon III, a science-fiction convention in 1981. In it a schoolgirl with a booster hidden in her backpack fights her way through the monsters and machines of classic science fiction. The team went on to found Gainax, the studio behind Evangelion. Who designed the girl?
context: Takami Akai designed and animated the girl, Hiroyuki Yamaga directed, and Hideaki Anno drew the machines, with Toshio Okada producing. In the Daicon IV opening of 1983 she returns grown up, in a bunny costume. The shorts used music and characters without permission, so they have never had an official release.

question: A Studio Ghibli producer signed a deal with Disney in 1996 to release most of the Japanese studio's films across North America through 2017, and Disney gave them new English dubs with Hollywood casts. But one famous Ghibli film was quietly left out of the deal. Which one?
context: Grave of the Fireflies was produced not by Ghibli but by the publisher Shinchosha, with Ghibli only providing the animation, so its rights were separate; Central Park Media and later Sentai Filmworks released it in the US. Disney distributed nearly every other Ghibli release in North America until GKIDS took over.

question: A well-known Power Rangers voice actor took the lead role of the biker gang leader when Pioneer Entertainment produced a brand new English dub of Akira in 2001, with a fresh cast. The first dub had opened in American theaters on December 25, 1989, and stayed the American standard for over a decade. Who voiced the gang leader in the 2001 dub?
context: Joshua Seth voiced Tetsuo in the 2001 dub. Bosch voiced Kaneda. The 1989 Streamline dub had Cam Clarke as Kaneda and Jan Rabson as Tetsuo. Steve Blum has said in interviews that he turned down a chance to audition for Kaneda in the Streamline dub because he was unsure how to play a teenage protagonist with that level of intensity.

question: DIC Entertainment, an American company, renamed most of the cast and cut several episodes when it dubbed the first two seasons of Usagi Tsukino's adventures for English TV, starting in 1995. It also hid one of the Japanese show's same-sex romances from young viewers. Which change did DIC make?
answer: The villain Zoisite was rewritten from a man into a woman
choices: The villain Zoisite was rewritten from a man into a woman
Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune were rewritten as cousins
Sailor Mars and Sailor Jupiter were rewritten as cousins
Sailor Venus and Sailor Mercury were rewritten as sisters
context: DIC's dub of the first two seasons made Zoisite a woman, which hid his romance with Kunzite (renamed Malachite). Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune first appear in the third season, which Cloverway dubbed in 2000, and that dub made them cousins. Viz Media's 2014 redub restored the original characters and relationships.

question: A Japanese art director painted the green fields, rainy roads and great camphor tree of My Neighbor Totoro in 1988, and his countryside became the look people picture when they think of Studio Ghibli. He went on to art-direct three more Ghibli films in the next ten years. Who was he?
context: Oga was art director of My Neighbor Totoro (1988), Only Yesterday (1991), Pom Poko (1994) and Princess Mononoke (1997), and much later of The Tale of the Princess Kaguya (2013). An exhibition of his work was called Kazuo Oga: The Man Who Drew Totoro's Forest.

question: An older manga artist took on an eighteen-year-old Kentaro Miura as an assistant, years before Berserk began, and soon let him go, saying there was nothing he could teach the young man that he did not already know. That artist went on to create one of the longest-running boxing manga ever printed. Who was he?
context: Miura worked briefly as an assistant to George Morikawa, later the creator of Hajime no Ippo, who sent him on his way because the teenager already knew everything Morikawa could teach. A few years later Miura's 48-page Berserk prototype won a prize in Hakusensha's ComiComi manga contest.

question: Freckled, green-haired Izuku Midoriya gets bullied at school in My Hero Academia, because he has no superpower in a world of Quirks. Other kids twist a Japanese word for 'useless' into a cruel nickname, though a friend later flips it to mean 'you can do it.' What is this nickname?
context: Izuku Midoriya was bullied by Katsuki Bakugo since childhood; Bakugo coined Deku as an insult meaning 'useless.' Ochaco Uraraka later reframed it as a hero name.

question: The world's number-one hero meets a powerless boy named Izuku Midoriya as My Hero Academia begins, and he chooses to pass his own superpower on to the boy. He is tall, blond and super-muscular, and his famous smile is meant to make everyone feel safe. What is the top hero's name?
context: All Might's true form is the gaunt Toshinori Yagi. The power he passes on is One For All, which came to him from his own teacher, its seventh holder.

question: A loud orphan in an orange jumpsuit, with whisker marks on his cheeks, carries a nine-tailed demon fox sealed inside him in Masashi Kishimoto's 1999 manga. He dreams of becoming his village's leader, the Hokage. What is his name?
context: The Nine-Tailed Fox, Kurama, was sealed inside the baby Naruto by the Fourth Hokage. Naruto's dream from page one is to become Hokage himself.

question: Monkey D. Luffy's body stretches and snaps back like rubber in Eiichiro Oda's manga One Piece, because when he was small he ate a strange magical fruit. It gave him this power but stole his ability to swim. What kind of fruit is that?
context: Luffy ate the Gomu Gomu no Mi (Gum-Gum Fruit) as a child. Devil Fruit eaters gain a unique power but lose the ability to swim — a major drawback for pirates.

question: A high-school boy with orange hair who can see ghosts meets a tiny Soul Reaper, Rukia Kuchiki, one night in Tite Kubo's Bleach. He takes her powers to save his family from a soul-eating monster and carries a huge sword. What is his name?
context: Bleach ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016. Ichigo's zanpakuto, Zangetsu, takes the form of a massive cleaver once he learns its name.

question: George Morikawa's boxing manga opens on a high-school boy who helps run his mother's fishing charter and is bullied every day. A young professional boxer rescues him and takes him to a gym, where the boy finds a terrifying punch. What is the boy's name?
context: Morikawa Jouji's manga began in 1989 and is still running, making it one of the longest sports manga in history. Ippo's mother runs a fishing-charter business.

question: The 2016 manga Demon Slayer sends a gentle charcoal-seller boy home to find that demons have killed his family. Only his sister Nezuko survives, half-turned into a demon herself. He joins the secret Demon Slayer Corps to find a cure. What is his name?
context: Koyoharu Gotouge's Kimetsu no Yaiba ran from 2016 to 2020 in Weekly Shonen Jump. Tanjiro carries a small wooden box on his back containing his demon sister Nezuko.

question: Satsuki and Mei move to the Japanese countryside in Hayao Miyazaki's 1988 movie and meet a huge, sleepy, grey forest spirit in the woods, one that no grown-up can see. One rainy night he waits beside them at a bus stop, and later they ride a grinning Catbus. What is his name, the one that gives the movie its title?
context: My Neighbor Totoro was released as a double feature with Takahata's Grave of the Fireflies. The two sisters Satsuki and Mei live in the countryside while their mother is in the hospital.

question: Ash Ketchum sets out in the 1997 Japanese anime to become a Pokemon Master, and Team Rocket comes after him and his partner: Jessie, James and a scheming Pokemon who walks upright on two legs and talks like a human. What is that talking cat called?
context: Meowth taught himself to walk and talk to impress a female Meowth named Meowzie. The Jessie-James-Meowth trio appears in nearly every episode of the original Indigo League series.

question: Akira Toriyama opened his 1984 manga Dragon Ball on a small boy alone in the mountains, with a red-tipped power pole, a monkey tail and an orange ball from his late Grandpa Gohan, one of seven wish-granting orbs. What is the boy's name?
context: Goku is a Saiyan from the planet Vegeta, sent to Earth as a baby. Toriyama based Dragon Ball loosely on the Chinese novel Journey to the West, with Goku as the Monkey King Sun Wukong.

question: Ryuk, a bored death-god, drops a black notebook out of the sky in the manga Death Note. Anyone whose name is written in it dies. A brilliant Tokyo schoolboy picks it up and decides to kill criminals in secret. What is his name?
context: Tsugumi Ohba wrote and Takeshi Obata illustrated Death Note from 2003 to 2006. The rules say any human whose name is written in the notebook will die, provided the writer knows the victim's face.

question: Hiromu Arakawa's manga sends Edward Elric and his younger brother into a forbidden experiment to bring their dead mother back to life. It costs Edward an arm and a leg and his brother his entire body. The government then makes Edward a State Alchemist and gives him a silver pocket watch and a famous nickname. What is the nickname?
context: Edward Elric is the youngest State Alchemist in Amestris history, certified at age twelve. His brother Alphonse's soul is bound to a hollow suit of armor after the same failed human transmutation.

question: A talking black cat named Luna tells Usagi Tsukino, a clumsy, cry-baby fourteen-year-old Tokyo schoolgirl, that she is really a reborn princess and has to save the world. Every time Usagi transforms she wears a schoolgirl sailor suit, and her friends soon transform too. What is Usagi's hero name?
context: Usagi Tsukino (renamed Serena in the English dub) gets her powers from a talking cat named Luna. The team grew through the series to include Sailors Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and later the outer planets.

question: Koyoharu Gotouge's manga Demon Slayer gives Tanjiro a jumpy blond fellow recruit who cries and shouts that he wants to run away. The moment he faints from fear mid-fight, his body moves on its own as a deadly Thunder Breathing master. What is his name?
context: Zenitsu can only execute the First Form of Thunder Breathing, but he does it at a speed no one else matches. He trained under Jigoro Kuwajima, a former Thunder Hashira.

question: Criminals across Japan start dropping dead of heart attacks in Death Note, and the police call in the world's greatest detective, a pale young man who crouches in his chair, eats cake and hides his real name. Which capital letter does he go by?
context: L Lawliet was raised at Watari's orphanage, Wammy's House, which also brought up Near and Mello. He communicates anonymously through Watari and refuses to show his face in public.

question: Hajime Isayama's Attack on Titan shuts the last of humanity behind three enormous stone walls, safe from man-eating Titans. Each wall carries a legendary queen's name, and the king and the royal capital sit inside the innermost. Which queen is that wall named for?
context: Hajime Isayama's manga began in 2009. The walls are named (outer to inner) Maria, Rose, Sina. The Survey Corps wing emblem became one of the most recognizable anime symbols of the 2010s.

question: A green-haired swordsman with a fearsome scowl and a black bandana wields three swords at the same time in Eiichiro Oda's One Piece, one in each hand and the third clenched between his teeth. He is Monkey D. Luffy's first mate. What is his name?
context: Zoro's three-sword style is called Santoryu. He carries the white-sheathed Wado Ichimonji, which belonged to his childhood friend Kuina. His lifelong goal is to become the world's greatest swordsman.
