question: A tough middle-school delinquent with a black slicked-back pompadour pushes a small boy out of a speeding car's path in Yoshihiro Togashi's Yu Yu Hakusho. He wakes up a ghost, and the spirit world offers to bring him back as a Spirit Detective. What is his name?
context: Yoshihiro Togashi's manga ran 1990 to 1994 in Weekly Shonen Jump. Yusuke is sent back to life by Koenma, the toddler son of King Yama, ruler of the Spirit World.

question: A cheerful twelve-year-old with spiky green hair leaves his aunt's home on tiny Whale Island in Yoshihiro Togashi's manga Hunter x Hunter. His father abandoned him as a baby, and the boy sets out alone to pass the deadly Hunter Exam and find him. What is the boy's name?
context: Yoshihiro Togashi (also Yu Yu Hakusho) began Hunter x Hunter in 1998. The manga is famous for years-long hiatuses due to Togashi's health. Gon's father Ging is one of the strongest Hunters alive.

question: AidaIro's manga Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun borrows a spot from real Japanese school ghost stories, the third stall of a girls' toilet, and puts a mischievous boy spirit in it. A girl summons him and calls him Hanako-kun, only a nickname. What is his human name?
context: AidaIro's manga began in Monthly GFantasy in 2014. Hanako-kun is one of the Seven Mysteries of Kamome Academy. His twin brother Tsukasa Yugi figures into the deeper plot of why he became a school spirit.

question: Hanako, the boy ghost of the third-floor girls' bathroom in Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, is summoned by a shy first-year who wants her crush to love her back. A mermaid's curse soon binds her to him as his assistant. What is her name?
context: Yashiro swallows a mermaid's scale and falls under the Mermaid's Curse; Hanako takes a scale from the same mermaid to share the curse, so she stays human unless she is soaked in water. The curse binds their souls.

question: A bored Gunma high-school boy takes his father's old black-and-white Toyota AE86 out before dawn to deliver tofu in Shuichi Shigeno's Initial D. His father has been secretly training him for years. When a hotshot street-racing crew comes to conquer Mount Akina, he quietly outdrives every one of them. What is the boy's name?
context: Shuichi Shigeno's manga began in 1995. Takumi's father Bunta is the one who really taught him by sending him on tofu deliveries up Mt. Akina from age 13, requiring he not spill a cup of water on the dashboard.

question: A tough Japanese delinquent discovers a star-shaped birthmark on his neck in 1988, in JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3, and finds he can summon a purple ghost-fighter he names Star Platinum. To save his dying mother he journeys to Egypt with his grandfather Joseph Joestar. What is this delinquent's name?
context: Hirohiko Araki's Stardust Crusaders ran 1989 to 1992. Jotaro's Stand, Star Platinum, is one of the most iconic in the series and shouts a rapid-fire battle cry while throwing a flurry of punches.

question: Team 7's teacher in Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto turns up late, lazy and silver-haired, with a racy orange paperback open in public and a red Sharingan eye hidden under his headband. That eye earned him the nickname Copy Ninja. What is his name?
context: Kakashi's covered left eye is a Sharingan, the copying eye that earned him the nickname Copy Ninja. The orange book he reads is Make-Out Paradise, written by Jiraiya.

question: A wild boy raised by boars in the mountains joins Tanjiro in Demon Slayer, wearing a boar's head as a mask and fighting with two chipped, jagged blades. He starts as a rival and becomes a friend. What is his name?
context: Inosuke wears the head of a wild boar over his own (surprisingly pretty) face. His Beast Breathing style is self-taught and includes finger-fang attacks.

question: A loud, angry boy in Class 1-A makes his palms sweat nitroglycerin and ignites it to blast enemies in Kohei Horikoshi's My Hero Academia. He screams insults, hates losing worse than dying, and grew up bullying Izuku Midoriya. What is this rival's name?
context: Bakugo's hero name became Dynamight, long after U.A. turned down his first idea, King Explosion Murder. He won the Sports Festival in Season 2 and was strapped to a pillar in restraints for the medal ceremony.

question: The villain of Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer hides in Tokyo disguised as a normal husband and father. He is the very first demon ever made, more than a thousand years old, and one direct ray of sun reduces him to ash. What is his name?
context: Muzan was created by a Heian-period doctor's experimental treatment to cure his illness. He spent a thousand years hunting the Blue Spider Lily, the only flower that could grant him immunity to sunlight.

question: An older brother in Hiromu Arakawa's manga binds the younger boy's soul to a giant, empty suit of armor with a blood seal, after a forbidden ritual to raise their dead mother takes the boy's entire body. Still gentle inside the cold hollow steel, the boy rescues stray cats everywhere he travels. What is his name?
context: The blood seal on the inside of the armor's neck is the only thing tying his soul to the metal.

question: A thirteen-year-old witch-in-training leaves home for a year as a rite of passage and flies on her broomstick to a European-style seaside town, where she starts a flying-package delivery service, in Studio Ghibli's 1989 film. Her only companion is a talkative black cat. What is the cat's name?
context: Kiki's Delivery Service was Miyazaki's adaptation of Eiko Kadono's children's novel. Tradition holds that all young witches must spend a year on their own training; Kiki picks Koriko, a Stockholm-like city.

question: Endeavor, the Number Two Hero of My Hero Academia, forces his small son to train nonstop. The boy reaches Class 1-A with a large burn scar over his left eye, and he can freeze things with his right side and burn things with his left. What is the boy's name?
context: Endeavor (Enji Todoroki) arranged his marriage to Shoto's mother specifically for her ice quirk, planning a child capable of surpassing All Might. The scar came from his mother throwing boiling water at him as a child.

question: The boxing gym in Hajime no Ippo has a hulking middleweight star whom the coach pulled out of street brawling. After weeks of only running and left jabs, with no sparring, he won his first professional bout in the first round. He mentors the shy high schooler Ippo. What is the big man's name?
context: Takamura fights his way up the weight classes, from the Japanese middleweight title to world belts at junior middleweight, middleweight and super middleweight, and he means to keep climbing to heavyweight. Coach Genji Kamogawa, a prizefighter in Japan just after the Second World War, found him as a street brawler and stepped in to stop him killing someone after noticing his powerful right.

question: Ippo unveils a signature move in George Morikawa's boxing manga Hajime no Ippo, weaving his upper body from side to side and slamming in hooks as it swings. The move borrows the name of a ferocious 1920s American heavyweight champion who bobbed and weaved the same way. What is it called?
context: Jack Dempsey held the world heavyweight title from 1919 to 1926, and his bobbing-and-weaving style made him a target that never stopped moving. Ippo first throws the move in a fight against Ponchai without even knowing what it is called.

question: Ufotable's 2020 film Mugen Train put one of Demon Slayer's nine Hashira, its elite swordsmen, aboard a haunted overnight train as its lead, and it beat Spirited Away's twenty-year record to become the highest-grossing Japanese film of all time. Which Hashira led it?
context: Mugen Train grossed over 40 billion yen, surpassing Spirited Away's 20-year record. The Upper Moon Three demon Akaza is Rengoku's opponent. Ufotable's animation drew international box-office attention to anime films.

question: A swordsman who rarely speaks spares Tanjiro and his demon sister Nezuko in chapter one of the manga Demon Slayer. He wears only half of a black-and-red kimono coat called a haori, has teal-colored eyes and serves as the Water Hashira, one of Japan's top nine demon-hunters. What is his name?
context: Water Breathing has ten forms, with Eleventh — Dead Calm — invented by Giyu himself. He wears a mismatched haori with half being the geometric pattern of his sister Tsutako's kimono and half his late friend Sabito's.

question: Masashi Kishimoto built the world of Naruto from five great ninja countries, each with a hidden village, and set his hero's home in the Land of Fire, under a cliff carved with the faces of every past Hokage. What is that village called?
answer: Konohagakure (the Village Hidden in the Leaves)
choices: Konohagakure (the Village Hidden in the Leaves)
context: The five Great Ninja Villages are Konoha, Kiri, Suna, Kumo and Iwa (Stone), and each is led by a Kage. Konoha's Kage is the Hokage, and the faces of its past Hokage are carved into the cliff above the village.

question: The wandering sage Jiraiya, one of three legendary ninja, trains Naruto in a signature move that spins a swirling ball of chakra energy in the palm. The village's Fourth Hokage invented it years earlier. What is the move called?
context: The Fourth Hokage designed the Rasengan as an unfinished technique he hoped to combine with an elemental nature. Naruto eventually completes it by adding his wind affinity, creating the Rasenshuriken.

question: Monkey D. Luffy hunts the legendary treasure Gol D. Roger left at the end of the Grand Line in Eiichiro Oda's pirate manga, which began in Weekly Shonen Jump in July 1997 and became the bestselling manga in history. What is this treasure called?
context: Gol D. Roger, the previous Pirate King, was executed publicly 22 years before the series begins. His final words mentioned his treasure being 'in one piece' at the end of the Grand Line. The Straw Hat crew sails to find it.

question: A long-bearded, scar-faced veteran founds the Gotei 13 a thousand years before Tite Kubo's Bleach opens: thirteen squads of Soul Reapers guarding the Soul Society, a feudal-Japan-style afterlife realm. When the series starts he is still their captain-commander. Who is he?
context: Yamamoto founded the Gotei 13 over a thousand years before the present-day story. His zanpakuto, Ryujin Jakka, is considered the strongest fire-type in the Soul Society. It is disguised as a wooden walking cane.

question: A small Tokyo studio sent the soldiers of Attack on Titan sky-diving through fluid Titan combat when Hajime Isayama's manga reached anime in 2013. It animated seasons 1 through 3 of the walled-city story, and a different studio later took over the final season. Which studio animated the first three?
context: Wit Studio handled Seasons 1-3. MAPPA took over for the Final Season starting in 2020 after Wit declined the heavy CGI work needed for the late-series titan scenes. Isayama originally pitched the manga to Weekly Shonen Jump and was rejected.

question: Wammy's House, the orphanage that raised the detective L, is bringing up two more gifted boys in the manga Death Note as candidates to follow him one day. One has white hair and eats marshmallows; the other is blond and loves chocolate. Who are they?
context: Near (Nate River) and Mello (Mihael Keehl) are the two top candidates Wammy's House raised to inherit the name L, and their rivalry drives the second half of the manga.

question: A tall woman with long dark hair and a red tattoo on her chest is the first Homunculus the Elric brothers meet in Hiromu Arakawa's manga. She is one of seven artificial humans they hunt, each named after one of the seven deadly sins of Christian tradition. Which sin is she named for?
context: Arakawa structured the seven homunculi-to-sins arrangement methodically: Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Envy, Sloth, Wrath, Pride. The 2009 Brotherhood adaptation follows her manga faithfully; the 2003 anime diverged at the halfway point with its own ending.

question: Gon takes a personality test in Yoshihiro Togashi's manga Hunter x Hunter: a drop of water floats, and what his aura does to it sorts him into one of the six styles of Nen, the life-energy every fighter wields. His style belongs to hot-headed, straightforward brawlers who solve every problem by hitting harder. What is Gon's Nen category called?
context: The six Nen categories are Enhancement (Gon, Uvogin), Emission (Franklin), Transmutation (Killua, Hisoka), Conjuration (Kurapika, Kortopi), Manipulation (Shalnark) and Specialization (Chrollo). Each person has one natural category.

question: Hirohiko Araki brought something new into JoJo's Bizarre Adventure with Part 3, Stardust Crusaders: ghostly fighting spirits, humanoid guardians of pure willpower that only some people can see or fight with. The whole series is now famous for them. What did Araki name them?
context: Parts 1 and 2 used Hamon, also called the Ripple, a power drawn from controlled breathing. Araki has said the idea of Stands came from wanting to draw the heart and soul, as the series moved from physical power to the spirit. Each Stand has its own name, such as Star Platinum or Magician's Red.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi sent his Spirit Detective into a brutal multi-day fighting contest between teams of humans and demons in Yu Yu Hakusho, hosted on an island and run by demon gangs who bet on the matches. It became the manga's most famous arc. What is that arc called?
context: The Dark Tournament pits Team Urameshi against one team after another, with rich demon gangs betting on every match.

question: Takumi races other drivers down Mt. Akina at night in his father's beat-up Toyota AE86, in Shuichi Shigeno's manga Initial D, set in Japan's Gunma Prefecture. Shigeno based the road on a real touge, a winding mountain-pass road. Which real mountain was it?
context: Shigeno based all the Initial D mountain courses on real Gunma touge routes. Akina = Haruna, Myogi = Myogi, Akagi = Akagi, Usui = Usui, Irohazaka = Irohazaka. Real drift drivers studied the manga in the late '90s and the routes became pilgrimage sites.

question: Takumi drifts his father's beat-up hatchback down mountain roads at night in Initial D, to a fast, thumping Italian dance style that grew famous with drift-race fans. Japan's music label Avex Trax released that music in a long-running album series under one name. What was it called?
context: Tracks like 'Deja Vu' by Dave Rodgers, 'Running in the 90s' by Max Coveri, and Manuel's high-speed driving anthem became Initial D signatures. Many of the artists were Italian musicians recording for the Japanese market only.

question: Ash Ketchum starts his whole journey at Professor Samuel Oak's laboratory the morning he turns ten, in the Pokemon anime that began on Japanese television in April 1997. His mother Delia and Oak, the local Pokemon researcher, both live in the place he leaves behind. Where is that?
context: The Japanese name is Masara Town. Professor Oak's research lab gives starter Pokemon to new ten-year-old trainers. Ash arrived too late on his tenth birthday and was given the unwanted, troublesome Pikachu, who refused to enter his Poke Ball.

question: Misty, the water-type gym leader of Cerulean City, faces Ash Ketchum for his second gym badge in the Pokemon anime. She is the youngest of four, and her three glamorous older siblings actually run the gym as a synchronized-swimming show. What does the show name the three of them?
context: Misty is the youngest of four sisters and is treated as the runt by the other three. Togepi, which hatches mid-series from an egg Ash found, becomes hers and one of the anime's most marketable characters.

question: Goku travels the world in Akira Toriyama's 1984 manga Dragon Ball, hunting seven glowing orange orbs that can make a single wish come true. Simply having all seven is not enough on its own. One special step brings the wish-granting dragon out. What action summons him?
answer: Calling the dragon Shenron by name with all seven balls together
choices: Calling the dragon Shenron by name with all seven balls together
Rubbing the strongest ball after midnight under the full moon
Burning a phoenix-feather offering in the seven balls' center
Chanting the secret name of King Kai over the assembled set
context: The seven Dragon Balls scatter across the planet after each wish, becoming inert orange stones for one Earth year. Bulma's invention, the Dragon Radar, lets her track them. Piccolo's Namekian variant has its own dragon, Porunga.

question: A maddened boar god attacks a small mountain village of the northern Emishi tribe in the opening scene of Hayao Miyazaki's 1997 film Princess Mononoke. The young prince who defends it takes a curse mark that spreads up his arm, and he rides west on a red elk searching for a cure. What is that prince's name?
context: Princess Mononoke was the highest-grossing film in Japan until Titanic released later that year. The Forest Spirit (the deer god Shishigami) and the wolf-raised San are the other central figures. Neil Gaiman wrote the English-dub adaptation.

question: Chihiro, a ten-year-old girl, signs a contract in a giant bathhouse for gods in Hayao Miyazaki's 2001 film, after her parents are magically turned into pigs. The owner is a tiny old witch with an enormous head, a huge hooked nose and jewelry dripping from every finger, and she sets Chihiro to scrubbing tubs in the boiler room. What is this witch's name?
context: Chihiro must take a new name (Sen) and forget her own to keep working. Yubaba's identical twin sister Zeniba lives at Swamp Bottom; the two characters are voiced by the same actress in both Japanese (Mari Natsuki) and English (Suzanne Pleshette).

question: A girl at Kamome Academy stumbles into the hauntings students whisper about in AidaIro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun: ghostly powers in seven places, from a girls' lavatory to a staircase by the art room. She gets tangled up with the friendly ghost of the third-floor bathroom. What are the seven hauntings called as a set?
context: Hanako-kun is the Seventh Mystery, of the girls' bathroom. Each of the Seven Mysteries has its own boundary, a source of power and a part of school life it controls. Some English versions call them the Seven Wonders.

question: A loud red-haired boy from a long family line of ghost- and spirit-hunters joins the gang around the bathroom ghost Hanako in AidaIro's manga Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun. He is training to be a hunter himself, and the spirit he has befriended is exactly the kind he must learn to banish. What is his name?
context: Kou's older brother Teru is the strongest active exorcist at Kamome Academy. Kou befriends Hanako-kun despite his family's mandate to exorcise him. Kou's later friendship with the false-mystery Mitsuba is a fan-beloved subplot.

question: The Flame Alchemist snaps his fingers in ignition-cloth gloves and burns his enemies to ash in Hiromu Arakawa's manga. His country makes its state alchemists soldiers, 'human weapons of the State,' and he wears the blue military uniform. He secretly plots to climb the military ladder, seize the office of Fuhrer and end the corrupt regime from the inside. What is his full name and army rank?
context: Mustang served in the Ishvalan genocide as a flame alchemist and is haunted by it. His secret long-game is to take the throne and dismantle the corrupt military. Arakawa drew the Ishvalan arc to evoke real-world ethnic-cleansing scenarios.

question: A blue-haired teenage girl from the city arrives on her motorbike where the wild boy Goku lives alone in the mountains. She carries a strange invention, the Dragon Radar, which pings whenever it detects one of seven magic orbs. Goku and the girl team up to hunt them. What is her name?
context: Bulma is the daughter of Dr. Brief, founder of Capsule Corp (Japan's most innovative inventor). Her name comes from the Japanese pronunciation of 'bloomers' (underwear); Toriyama named all the Briefs family after underwear. She eventually marries Vegeta.

question: Ash Ketchum leaves town with his stubborn partner in the Pokemon anime and, on Route 1, catches his first wild Pokemon: a small green bug. It will later evolve twice into the Butterfree he tearfully sets free in a famous Season 1 goodbye. What kind of Pokemon does he catch?
context: Ash catches Caterpie in episode 3, Ash Catches a Pokemon, and a Pidgeotto later in the same episode. The release episode, Bye Bye Butterfree, is episode 21 and left a generation of late-1990s children in tears.

question: The number-one hero of My Hero Academia passes a rare inherited Quirk, stronger with each generation, to Izuku Midoriya. It began with two brothers who fought bitterly in the earliest days of Quirks: one could steal Quirks and hoard them, the other could pass a single Quirk down the generations. What are the two rival powers called?
answer: One For All and All For One
choices: One For All and All For One
context: All For One could steal Quirks and stockpile them. He forced a power-stockpiling Quirk on his younger brother, and it merged with the brother's own small Quirk for passing powers on: the result was One For All, which each holder makes stronger before handing it down.

question: Ippo faces a boxer from Osaka known as the Naniwa Tiger in the most personal title fight of Hajime no Ippo. The man's signature Smash, a hook from a crouch, knocked Ippo down in an earlier match, and the two grow to respect each other. Who is Ippo's title-fight opponent?
context: Sendo first appears as a heel, mocking Ippo before their first fight. He later holds the Japanese featherweight title, and his finishing blow, the Smash, is a hook thrown from a crouch. Morikawa named a real Osaka boxer, Hidekazu Akai, nicknamed the Naniwa Rocky, as one model for him.

question: Tanjiro trains under a tall, blind warrior hung with prayer beads during the Hashira Training Arc of Demon Slayer. He is the Stone Hashira, one of nine who each master a unique Breathing Style, and he is considered the strongest among the active pillars. What is his name?
context: Gyomei was nearly executed in his civilian life after killing demons that attacked the orphanage he tended; the law refused to believe demons existed. Stone Breathing has five forms. He fights with a flail-and-axe weapon connected by a chain, used together with bead-prayers.

question: The Akatsuki, nine rogue ninja in black cloaks patterned with red clouds, make their opening move in Naruto Shippuden, two and a half years after the first series, with Naruto now a teenager. They kidnap a red-haired figure from the desert, a former enemy who has since become one of his dearest friends. Who do they take?
context: Gaara carries the One-Tailed beast, Shukaku, sealed inside him, which is why the Akatsuki, who hunt the tailed beasts, come for him. His kidnapping launches the rescue mission that opens Shippuden.

question: Young Monkey D. Luffy worships a crew of pirates who drink at the local bar in Windmill Village in Eiichiro Oda's One Piece. Before they sail away, their captain hands the boy his own treasured straw hat, on one condition: Luffy must become a great pirate someday and bring it back to him. Who is that captain?
context: Shanks gives Luffy his straw hat before leaving Windmill Village, on the condition that Luffy becomes a great pirate and returns it. The same chapter has Shanks lose his left arm saving the boy from a Sea King, a monstrous sea beast.

question: Hajime Isayama showed his early pages of Attack on Titan, the story of humans huddled behind stone walls, to the editors of the most famous boys' weekly in Japan. They told him to change his style to suit their magazine. He refused, walked away and took the story to Kodansha instead. Which magazine did he walk away from?
context: Isayama first took the story to Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump in 2006, and its editors asked him to rework his style to fit the magazine. He declined and went to Kodansha, which launched Attack on Titan in its monthly Bessatsu Shonen Magazine in September 2009.

question: The high schooler Light sets out in the manga Death Note to murder criminals worldwide from behind his school desk, with a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it. To keep his identity hidden he picks a nickname that bends an English word into Japanese sounds. What do the detective L and the news channels end up calling him?
context: 'Kira' is a romanization of the English word 'killer' transliterated through Japanese phonetics. Light adopts it as the persona under which he claims to be God of the new world. The Kira name becomes shorthand among investigators and a cult-following emerges in-universe.

question: The Elric brothers try to bring their mother back with human transmutation, alchemy's ultimate taboo. The rebound costs Edward an arm and a leg and takes his brother's whole body. At the moment of failure they meet something that shows the source of alchemy. What do they meet?
answer: The Gate of Truth, with the entity called Truth at its threshold
choices: The Gate of Truth, with the entity called Truth at its threshold
The Philosopher's Stone, dissolved in their mother's blood
The shadow of their father Hohenheim, watching silently
The homunculus Envy, disguised as their mother
context: Truth is a faceless white figure who personally collects the 'toll' for human-transmutation attempts. The Gate of Truth contains all knowledge of alchemy and the universe's structure. Each alchemist who sees the Gate is taking a piece of forbidden knowledge with terrible cost.

question: Gon and Killua, twelve-year-old friends, finish the Hunter Exam and head for a towering martial-arts building where fighters climb the floors one bout at a time. There a soft-spoken master named Wing teaches them Nen, the life-energy behind every fight in Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter x Hunter. What is that tower called?
context: Gon and Killua travel to Heavens Arena, a towering martial-arts arena, where they climb its floors and train under Wing, the master who teaches them Nen. The arc runs from chapter 44 to chapter 63 of the manga.

question: Jotaro and his globe-trotting grandfather Joseph Joestar race from Tokyo to Egypt in fifty days in JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3, to save Jotaro's mother. Jotaro is cool, laconic and hard to impress, and both his finger-pointing pose and his grumbled yare yare daze, or good grief, come from Hirohiko Araki's favourite screen tough guy. Which actor did Araki model Jotaro on?
context: Araki modelled Jotaro on Clint Eastwood, poses and catchphrases included: the pointing pose comes from Eastwood holding a .44 Magnum, and yare yare daze imitates the kind of lines Eastwood said in his films.

question: A delinquent comes back from the dead as a Spirit Detective in Yoshihiro Togashi's manga Yu Yu Hakusho and learns one signature move. He levels his index finger, gathers his spirit energy into the tip and lets it go as a single crackling blast. What is the move called?
context: The Spirit Gun, or Rei Gun, is a shot of spirit energy that Yusuke fires from his index finger, and it is his signature technique. He develops it with guidance from Botan, the ferry girl of the Spirit World.

question: Shuichi Shigeno began Initial D in 1995 with Takumi behind the wheel of a panda-colored Toyota Trueno, a car already ten years old and discontinued. Fans took its chassis code and turned it into a popular slang nickname. What is that nickname?
context: AE86 is the chassis code. The panda color scheme, white top and black bottom, became one of car culture's most recognized liveries. The AE86 went on to inspire the Toyota 86 of 2012, and the show's fame still pushes up the price of a used AE86. Takumi's father Bunta drove the original.

question: A pink, balloon-round Jigglypuff follows Ash and his friends from town to town in the Pokemon anime, desperate for someone to sing to. Its lullaby puts everyone who hears it fast asleep before the song is over, and Jigglypuff takes this as a terrible insult. What does Jigglypuff do to the sleeping audience?
answer: It scribbles on their faces with its marker
choices: It scribbles on their faces with its marker
It steals the food from their backpacks
It sticks flower petals in their hair
It rolls over them like a beach ball
context: Jigglypuff's song puts everyone who hears it to sleep, and when it notices, it angrily uses its marker, which doubles as its microphone, to draw on their faces.

question: Dr. Gero builds the android Cell as the ultimate weapon in Dragon Ball Z, assembling him from the cells of all the Z Fighters and beyond. To achieve his perfect form, Cell must absorb two earlier-model androids. Which two does he hunt and absorb?
context: Androids 17 and 18 are originally human siblings (Lapis and Lazuli) who were kidnapped by Dr. Gero and converted. Cell's Perfect Form, achieved by absorbing them both, makes him sleeker, more confident, and proportionally more powerful — the arc's iconic design moment.

question: Majin Buu, the strange pink demon sealed away centuries earlier by the old Supreme Kais, proves too strong for adult Goku's normal punches and energy beams in Dragon Ball Z. Goku's ultimate weapon is a giant blue ball of energy, charged by asking all living beings on Earth to raise their hands and pour their life energy into one attack. What is that signature attack called?
choices: The Big Bang Attack (Bigu Ban Atakku)
context: Goku first learns the Spirit Bomb from King Kai during the Saiyan arc. It uses borrowed energy and requires the donor's consent. In the Buu arc, Vegeta and others must convince Earth's population to raise their hands — a famously emotional moment as Hercule (Mr. Satan) leads the request.

question: Tanjiro and the others on the Mugen Train watch an Upper Moon, one of the top ranks of Muzan's twelve demon lieutenants, take on their Hashira at the climax of the story. The demon fights barehanded like a martial artist and urges the Hashira to become a demon too. Which Upper Moon is he?
context: Akaza fights with fists and kicks rather than a blade, and he admires strong fighters enough to want them made into demons. His duel with the Flame Hashira is the climax of the Mugen Train film.

question: A young man with dry, cracked skin gives the orders to the villains of My Hero Academia, and whatever he touches crumbles. His mentor, the first thief of Quirks, sits sealed inside a high-tech prison. What is the leader's name?
context: Tomura is the grandson of Nana Shimura, the seventh holder of One For All before All Might. He was raised by All For One after his Quirk, Decay, killed his family. The severed hands he wears on his face and body are among the series' most recognisable images.

question: Genji Kamogawa, the gruff coach of Hajime no Ippo, shares a fierce rivalry with an American soldier in a long flashback to the postwar occupation of Japan, in the late 1940s. The arrogant officer fells Kamogawa's friend Nekota with an illegal rabbit punch, leaving him brain-damaged, and Kamogawa strikes back with his Iron Fist. What is that American soldier's name?
context: Ralph Anderson is the arrogant American officer of the post-war flashback. He leaves Kamogawa's friend Ginpachi Nekota with permanent brain damage through an illegal rabbit punch, and Kamogawa answers him with his fearsome but self-destructive Tekken, the Iron Fist.

question: Yoriichi Tsugikuni, a Sengoku-era warrior and the greatest demon slayer who ever lived, mastered one sword style long ago in the manga Demon Slayer. Water Breathing, Flame Breathing, Thunder Breathing and the rest branched off from it, each modeled on an element or an animal's movement. What is that first, original style called?
context: Yoriichi Tsugikuni, the original swordsman, invented Sun Breathing and was the only person ever to develop the Demon Slayer Mark naturally. Tanjiro's family preserved the original Sun Breathing as a religious dance called Hinokami Kagura, taught from father to son in secret.

question: Goku looks up at a full moon in Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball, and his furry tail sets off a wild rampaging change he cannot control, big enough to crush houses. Toriyama loosely based the kid hero on Sun Wukong of the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West, tail included. What does Goku turn into?
answer: A giant ape called the Oozaru, hundreds of feet tall
choices: A giant ape called the Oozaru, hundreds of feet tall
A giant flame-breathing tiger called the Konjishi
A dragon-headed warrior called the Ryusenjin
context: Saiyans transform into Oozaru under any moon's reflected sunlight, increasing their power roughly tenfold but losing most rational control. Vegeta's tail is also cut off; eventually almost all Saiyans on Earth lose their tails. The Great Ape transformation appears one last time in DBZ Cell arc through Cell Junior.

question: Students at Kamome Academy whisper that stepping on the fourth step of the Misaki Stairs, in front of the art room, sends a person into the spirit world, in AidaIro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun. Like every school ghost story there, the rumor hides a real spirit who rules the stairs. What is that spirit?
answer: A fox spirit from an Inari shrine statue
choices: A fox spirit from an Inari shrine statue
A cursed mannequin from the art room
A drowned student from the school pool
context: The spirit of the Misaki Stairs is Yako, a fox spirit from an Inari statue who fell in love with a teacher named Misaki; her source of power is a pair of cutting shears he gave her. Each of the Seven Mysteries has its own boundary that holds its power.

question: Masashi Kishimoto wanted his loud orange-clad hero to have a childish catchphrase, so he gave the boy dattebayo, a sound with no real dictionary meaning that just makes him sound like a brat demanding attention. The English dub of the early anime had to put something in its place. What phrase did the dub use?
context: Kishimoto wanted a childlike catchphrase for Naruto, and dattebayo came to mind. The first episodes of the English dub replaced it with Believe it!, and later episodes swapped that for You know?

question: A substitute Soul Reaper and his friends invade the Soul Society in the second big arc of Tite Kubo's Bleach. They mean to rescue a captured comrade before her execution, and they storm the prison that holds her. What is that place called?
context: The Soul Society arc fills volumes 9 to 21 of the manga and more than 40 anime episodes. Rukia is held in the Senzaikyu, the Tower of Penitence, and the race to reach her before her execution ends on one of Bleach's most-discussed cliffhangers.

question: Eiichiro Oda sorted the cursed fruits of One Piece, which give strange powers but cost the eater the ability to swim forever, into three groups: Paramecia for weird body powers like Luffy's rubber stretch, Zoan for turning into animals, and a third, the rarest and strongest. What is that third group called?
context: Logia users can transform their bodies into and control an element — fire (Ace), magma (Akainu), light (Kizaru), darkness (Blackbeard). They're functionally immune to most physical attacks unless the opponent has Armament Haki or Sea-Prism Stone. Only a few dozen are known by the series' early arcs.

question: The detective L crouches on his heels over a slice of cake and works another case under another alias in Death Note. Only a handful of people know his real name, because any Death Note holder could kill him by using it. What is his real name?
context: L is the world's top three detectives all rolled into one anonymous identity. Watari (Quillsh Wammy) is his handler and the founder of Wammy's House orphanage that produces his successor candidates. The name never appears in the story itself; it was first printed in the official guidebook, Death Note 13: How to Read.

question: Hiromu Arakawa drew the Elric brothers' homeland to look like early-1900s Germany, with alchemy in place of gunpowder and state alchemists serving as soldiers. What is that country named?
context: The bordering nations Aerugo, Drachma, Creta and, to the east, Xing form the surrounding political landscape.

question: Studio Lerche made the 2020 anime of AidaIro's Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun, the manga about ghost stories haunting a Japanese school, and it aired from January to March of that year. Every episode opened on the same song. What was that opening theme called?
choices: Tentai Kansoku by Bump of Chicken
context: No.7 is performed by Jibaku Shounen Band, a name drawn from the series' Japanese title, Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun; the ending theme, Tiny Light, is sung by Akari Kito. Lerche animated the series.

question: Goku willingly holds his brother Raditz still at the start of Dragon Ball Z's Saiyan arc while a rival fires a beam through both of them. The rival is a longtime enemy of Goku turned reluctant ally, and the blast ends Goku's life along with his brother's. Who fires the beam?
context: Piccolo's Special Beam Cannon (Makankosappo) is the only technique strong enough to pierce Raditz's armor in that scene. Both Goku and Raditz die. Piccolo's redemption arc — from Demon King's son to mentor of Goku's son Gohan — is one of DBZ's most beloved character developments.

question: The first-years of Class 1-A fought it out at U.A. High's Sports Festival in Season 2 of My Hero Academia, in a final tournament that crowned one of them top first-year combatant. Who won the tournament?
answer: Katsuki Bakugo, who was strapped to a pillar for the medal ceremony
choices: Katsuki Bakugo, who was strapped to a pillar for the medal ceremony
Shoto Todoroki, who refused to use his fire side until the final
Izuku Midoriya, who broke both his arms beating Shinso
Tenya Iida, who used his engine-quirk Recipro Burst to clinch it
context: Bakugo refused to accept the title gracefully, because he had wanted to beat Todoroki at full power, and it became one of the series' defining character beats. The restraints on the medal podium became a fan meme.

question: Shota Aizawa, the strict homeroom teacher of Class 1-A in Kohei Horikoshi's manga My Hero Academia, cancels other people's Quirks just by staring at them. His civilian name hides a Japanese-word pun that points directly at what he does in a fight. How does his name carry the pun?
answer: His given name Shota is written with the kanji for 'erase'
choices: His given name Shota is written with the kanji for 'erase'
His given name Shota is written with the kanji for 'stare'
His family name Aizawa is written with the kanji for 'eye'
His family name Aizawa is written with the kanji for 'seal'
context: Shota is written 消太, and its first kanji, 消, is the one in kesu, 'to erase'. His hero name is Eraser Head, and his Quirk, Erasure, works only while he keeps his eyes open. His capture weapon is a scarf of cloth woven over steel wire.

question: The hulking middleweight star of the Kamogawa gym heads up into the mountains of Niigata on a training trip in George Morikawa's Hajime no Ippo. Out in the woods he ends up in a real fight, far from any ring or referee, and comes away with deep gouges across his chest and arms. What does he fight?
context: Takamura fights a mother bear on a mountain training trip and beats it by punching it again and again in the forehead, which earns him the name the Bear Slayer.

question: Readers of Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto picked up a demon-fighting manga called 666 Satan, published in English as O-Parts Hunter, and saw how much its art looked like his. Some accused one artist of copying the other. The explanation was simple: the creator of 666 Satan had been drawing manga at Masashi's side since early childhood. Who was he to Masashi?
context: Seishi Kishimoto, the creator of 666 Satan, is Masashi's identical twin brother. The two have drawn manga together since early childhood, and Seishi has said the similarities are not intentional but come from sharing so many of the same influences.

question: A fighter in Eiichiro Oda's One Piece exerts his will, and weaker men drop unconscious. He is using Haki, the story's system of willpower: beyond defensive Armament and perceptive Observation lies a rare third type, usable by only about one in a million people. What is that third type called?
answer: Conqueror's Haki (Haoshoku Haki / Color of the King)
choices: Conqueror's Haki (Haoshoku Haki / Color of the King)
Emperor's Haki (Yonkō Haki / Color of the Throne)
Pirate-King's Haki (Kaizoku Ō Haki / Color of the Crown)
Dragon's Haki (Ryūou Haki / Color of the World)
context: Conqueror's Haki is innate: it cannot be trained, only awakened, and its holders can knock out weaker people just by exerting it. Roger, Shanks and Luffy all have it.

question: Levi, the short, scowling Survey Corps captain of Attack on Titan, owes his compact build to a masked vigilante Hajime Isayama saw in the 2009 film of Alan Moore's graphic novel Watchmen, by Isayama's own account. Isayama made Levi spotless, as a contrast to that character's grubbiness. Which Watchmen character was it?
context: Isayama modelled Levi on Rorschach from Watchmen after watching the film adaptation, giving him a similar build but making him obsessed with cleanliness as a contrast to Rorschach's grubbiness. Levi leads an elite squad within the Survey Corps.

question: L meets Light face to face for the first time at a university entrance ceremony in Death Note, where both are named the top scorer. L introduces himself under a false name, lifted as a joke from a Japanese pop singer, and their cat-and-mouse rivalry begins. Which university hosts that meeting?
answer: To-Oh University, fictional Tokyo Imperial-style elite institution
choices: To-Oh University, fictional Tokyo Imperial-style elite institution
Tokyo University (Todai), the real-world institution Light secretly attends
Kanto Hogan University, the elite criminology-program school
Daikoku University, the fictional analogue to Kyoto Imperial
context: Light entered To-Oh under his own name; L appeared as the alias 'Hideki Ryuga' (sharing a name with a real Japanese pop star, a deliberate Ohba joke). The entrance ceremony scene where L whispers 'I am L' to Light became one of the manga's most-iconic two-page spreads.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi began Hunter x Hunter in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1998, and a fellow manga artist pitched in on the grey shading of the first volume, laying screentone on its single-color pages. Early in 1999 she married him. She was already famous in her own right for a magical-girl series about a clumsy schoolgirl who fights evil. Which series did she create?
context: Naoko Takeuchi, the creator of Sailor Moon, helped apply screentone to the single-color pages of Hunter x Hunter's first volume. She married Togashi on 6 January 1999.

question: Josuke Higashikata and his friends keep stumbling on strange spirit-fighters among the neighbours in Morioh, the quiet seaside town of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 4. Hirohiko Araki traded the world tour of Part 3 for this one place, and he modelled it on a real city, the one where he himself grew up. Which city?
context: Morioh is modelled on a part of Sendai in Miyagi Prefecture, Araki's hometown, and in 2012 a big JoJo exhibition opened there. Part 4 ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from May 1992 to December 1995.

question: Matsuko Mawatari released a bouncy pop single in November 1992, the opening theme of Yu Yu Hakusho, Studio Pierrot's hit TV anime of the Yoshihiro Togashi manga about a delinquent turned Spirit Detective. Its title translates as Smile Bomb. What is the song's Japanese title?
context: Hohoemi no Bakudan, Japanese for Smile Bomb, is a 1992 single by Matsuko Mawatari that became the opening theme of the Yu Yu Hakusho anime. Studio Pierrot made the series with Fuji Television and Yomiko Advertising, and Togashi ended the manga in 1994, exhausted by the weekly schedule.

question: Claire Danes voiced San in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's Princess Mononoke (1997), and a famous actor voiced Okkoto, the blind old chief of the boar clan. It was a famously huge production, with about 144,000 hand-drawn frames, and Hayao Miyazaki himself drew or retouched nearly 80,000 of them. Who voiced Okkoto?
answer: Keith David, the actor known for his deep growling voice work
choices: Keith David, the actor known for his deep growling voice work
Liam Neeson, fresh off his Schindler's List performance
Patrick Stewart, the actor known for Star Trek
Billy Bob Thornton, who also played the monk Jigo
context: Neil Gaiman wrote the English script, and the Miramax deal barred any cuts to the film. Toshio Suzuki, not Miyazaki, sent Harvey Weinstein the katana with its note, No cuts. John DiMaggio voiced Nago, the cursed boar of the opening, and Gillian Anderson voiced the wolf goddess Moro.

question: Goku fights the space tyrant Frieza on Planet Namek in a showdown that Akira Toriyama's manga says lasts five minutes. The anime was running faster than Toriyama could draw new chapters, so the animators stretched the fight with filler: energy-charging, scowling and repeated flashbacks. About how many weekly TV episodes did they spread those five minutes over?
answer: Roughly 19 episodes, spread across about half a year of weekly broadcast
choices: Roughly 19 episodes, spread across about half a year of weekly broadcast
Roughly 12 episodes, the standard 'major-arc' length of late-80s anime
Roughly 30 episodes, the most-padded fight in DBZ history
Roughly 7 episodes, surprisingly faithful to the manga's pace
context: The 'five minutes that lasted half a year' became a meme even at the time. The reason: Namek's planet-destruction countdown was set at five minutes of real time, which the anime stretched to allow Toriyama to keep up with his manga pace. The actual planet-destruction shockwave was eventually filmed to dramatic effect.

question: The anime team behind Dragon Ball GT (Grand Tour) invented material of their own when the show began airing in Japan in 1996, with no manga left to follow after Akira Toriyama's original had ended. They gave Goku a fresh transformation covered in red fur from head to toe, with his Saiyan tail grown back and his hair once again jet black. What is that new form called?
context: Super Saiyan 4 was designed by Tadayoshi Yamamuro, Dragon Ball's chief animation director. The form bypasses the gold-haired SSJ aesthetic for red fur and a Mohawk-style mane, returning to the Saiyans' Great Ape-tied roots. The form is non-canonical to Toriyama's later Dragon Ball Super continuity but remains beloved.

question: Tite Kubo first armed his Soul Reapers with guns, not the named blades called zanpakuto that they carry in Bleach. The project carried a gun-flavoured working title that was still in use when the series was first announced, until the guns became swords late in development. What was that working title?
context: Kubo's early Soul Reapers used guns, so the project was first called Snipe; he switched to swords late in development and later weighed titles such as Black and White before settling on Bleach. Jump rejected the first proposal, and Akira Toriyama, the creator of Dragon Ball, later wrote Kubo a letter of encouragement after reviewing the concept.

question: Eiichiro Oda said his love of pirates went back to a cartoon he watched as a small boy, a German-Japanese animated series about a clever little boy who gets his father's burly crew out of trouble with brains instead of muscle. Watching it, Oda realised that such men are a kind of pirate. Which series got him hooked?
context: Oda has said his interest in pirates was probably sparked by the anime Vicky the Viking, which taught him that Vikings are a type of pirate. Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball was his biggest influence as an artist.

question: Masashi Kishimoto tried his hero out in a single one-shot story in the summer 1997 issue of Akamaru Jump, before the weekly run of 1999 began. That first Naruto was not yet an orphan ninja with a demon sealed inside him. What was the hero of the 1997 one-shot?
answer: A young fox spirit posing as a human boy
choices: A young fox spirit posing as a human boy
A boy raised by wolves in a mountain shrine
A runaway samurai's son hiding in a temple
A toad summoner's apprentice in the hills
context: Kishimoto's one-shot in the summer 1997 issue of Akamaru Jump starred a young fox spirit who passes himself off as a human boy named Naruto. An even earlier idea, never printed, would have made Naruto a chef.

question: Hirohiko Araki, a lifelong rock fan, named most of the later fighting spirits of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure after songs and bands, so many that English releases rename some of them. Part 3 drew its names from somewhere else: Star Platinum, Magician's Red, and The World, the spirit of the vampire Dio Brando. Where do those names come from?
answer: The cards of the tarot's Major Arcana
choices: The cards of the tarot's Major Arcana
The signs of the Western zodiac
The constellations of the night sky
The planets of the solar system
context: Most Stands in Part 3 take a tarot card: Star Platinum is the Star, Magician's Red the Magician, and Dio's The World the twenty-first card of the Major Arcana. Later in the journey, nine enemies take the names of Egyptian gods. From Part 4 on, most Stands are named for songs, albums and bands, and English releases rename several to avoid copyright trouble.

question: Killua Zoldyck, twelve years old, runs away from home in Yoshihiro Togashi's manga Hunter x Hunter to become a Hunter. His family, the world's most feared assassins, keep an estate on Kukuroo Mountain, and anyone who slips in by the small side door instead of pushing open the massive doors of its outer gate meets the family's huge guardian. What waits there?
context: Mike, the largest of the Zoldyck guard dogs, kills intruders who come in without opening the Testing Gate, whose doors weigh tons apiece. Zebro, who looks like the gatekeeper, is really the man who cleans up after him.

question: John Siegler and John Loeffler wrote a power-rock theme song for the Pokemon anime, with David Rolfe on guitar, and it reached American television on September 7, 1998, with the episode 'Pokemon, I Choose You!' A generation of kids learned its shouted promise, Gotta catch 'em all, by heart. Which singer belted out the vocals?
context: Jason Paige sang the Pokemon Theme, written by John Siegler and John Loeffler, with David Rolfe on guitar. It premiered with the first English episode, Pokemon, I Choose You!, on September 7, 1998, and was the theme of the Indigo League season.

question: Goku shocks everyone in the final fight of the Cell Games by stepping aside and pushing his son Gohan forward. Cell hosts the tournament in Dragon Ball Z to show off his perfect form, and father and son have trained together in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber. Why does Goku step aside?
answer: Goku has determined Gohan has greater untapped potential and a hidden form Cell hasn't seen
choices: Goku has determined Gohan has greater untapped potential and a hidden form Cell hasn't seen
Goku has secretly absorbed a fatal disease and saves his strength for the wish-revival
Goku has decided to die in the tournament to let Gohan inherit the family role of Earth's defender
Goku has been Saiyan-cursed by Vegeta's secret bargain and cannot win the fight
context: Gohan goes Super Saiyan 2 for the first time in the Cell Games after Cell crushes Android 16's last words. The transformation, animated by Mitsuo Hashimoto, became one of DBZ's most iconic moments. Gohan's Cell-decimating Kamehameha was set up by Goku from the other side; the father-son combo move is one of the franchise's most emotional sequences.

question: Disney hired a big Hollywood cast when it produced the English dub of Hayao Miyazaki's 2004 film of Diana Wynne Jones's fantasy novel about a walking castle. One of that cast was a famous American stand-up comedian. Which comedian was it, and what was his part in the dub?
answer: Billy Crystal, who voiced the fire demon Calcifer
choices: Billy Crystal, who voiced the fire demon Calcifer
Robin Williams, who voiced the scarecrow Turnip Head
Eddie Murphy, who voiced the wheezing dog Heen
Steve Martin, who voiced the warring kingdom's King
context: Crystal had to fit his lines to animation that was already finished. The English dub also included Christian Bale (Howl), Emily Mortimer (young Sophie), Jean Simmons (old Sophie) and Lauren Bacall (the Witch of the Waste).

question: Goku and Gohan train in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber, a pocket world inside Kami's Lookout, the palace above Korin Tower, where one Earth day equals a full year of training. Only two trainees can enter at once, and each person has a lifetime cap. What is that lifetime entry limit?
answer: Two cumulative days (two years of training) total per person across a lifetime
choices: Two cumulative days (two years of training) total per person across a lifetime
One cumulative day (one year of training) total per person across a lifetime
Three cumulative days (three years of training) total per person across a lifetime
One year of training maximum per individual entrance, no lifetime cap
context: The two-day lifetime rule is established early but interpreted loosely later in the series. The chamber's environment — 50x Earth gravity, harsh temperature extremes, no horizon — makes survival difficult. The chamber was destroyed by Super Buu in the Buu arc, eliminating the franchise's deus-ex-machina training tool for later arcs.

question: The orange-clad hero of Masashi Kishimoto's manga cannot get enough of the noodles at Ichiraku Ramen, his favourite stall in the Hidden Leaf Village. Kishimoto took the boy's own name, a joke about that appetite, from one ramen topping: a slice of white fish cake with a pink spiral running through it, often laid on top of the noodles. What is that topping called?
context: Naruto's name derives from narutomaki, the swirled fish cake used as a ramen topping, which suits a boy who lives on Ichiraku's noodles. His family name, Uzumaki, is the Japanese word for a spiral or whirlpool.

question: Takeshi Obata drew Light and L in one of the most famous sequences of Death Note, each studying the other for a tell, with the thoughts of both men running side by side. The two had been monitoring each other's behavior for weeks. What was the activity at the heart of the scene?
answer: A hard-fought tennis match the two men play against each other
choices: A hard-fought tennis match the two men play against each other
An informal chess game between Light and Soichiro Yagami at L's invitation
A car ride from To-Oh to Light's home with Watari at the wheel
A surveillance-camera review with Light helping L with the case
context: The tennis sequence is famously voiced in inner monologue, with both Light and L providing first-person commentary on what they're observing about the other. Obata's drawing style on this sequence — close-ups of eyes, the ball, the racket — became defining for the manga's psychological-thriller register. L proposes the match soon after he first introduces himself to Light at the university entrance ceremony.

question: Nobuhiro Watsuki had a nineteen-year-old Eiichiro Oda on his team and credited the young assistant with helping create one of the characters in his hit samurai manga, about a wandering swordsman who carries a reverse-blade sword and has sworn never to kill again. Oda learned the trade this way, as an assistant to other manga artists, before he began One Piece. Which samurai manga was it?
context: Oda assisted on Shinobu Kaitani's Suizan Police Gang and Masaya Tokuhiro's Jungle King Tar-chan before joining Rurouni Kenshin at nineteen. Nobuhiro Watsuki credits him with helping create the character Honjo Kamatari.

question: Todoroki, son of the hero Endeavor, has half-ice and half-fire powers in My Hero Academia, and for years he refuses to use the fire half because his cruel father forced it on him through abusive training. During his first year at hero school one moment finally breaks through, and he lights up his left side. What changes his mind?
answer: Deku's heart-to-heart with him during their Sports Festival fight
choices: Deku's heart-to-heart with him during their Sports Festival fight
His first hospital visit in years to the mother who scarred him
Endeavor's near-death fight with the High-End Nomu
Stain's attack on Iida's brother, the hero Ingenium
context: The Sports Festival fight between Deku and Todoroki, in the tournament's second round, is one of the series' defining episodes. Bleeding, with his fingers broken, Deku convinced Todoroki that his fire was his own, not his father's.

question: The sleepy homeroom teacher of Class 1-A in My Hero Academia stares at a foe without blinking to shut off his Quirk, but sooner or later he has to blink. For those seconds Shota Aizawa carries a signature weapon that lets him restrain enemies at a distance. What is that weapon?
answer: His capture weapon — a binding scarf of steel-wire-cored cloth
choices: His capture weapon — a binding scarf of steel-wire-cored cloth
A pair of armored gauntlets — with retractable wire-launchers in each palm
A monofilament whip — coiled around his belt and weighted at the tip
A modified bullwhip — braided from carbon-aramid fiber with handle grips
context: Aizawa's Quirk, Erasure, cancels other Quirks while he keeps eye contact, and his dry eyes force him to blink, which limits how long he can use it. His capture weapon gives him a fighter's option in the seconds between cancels: it hangs from his neck like a scarf at rest and binds a foe in a fight.

question: George Morikawa did his research for Hajime no Ippo ringside, watching live fights at venues such as Tokyo's Korakuen Hall. He began the boxing manga, 'The First Step,' in Weekly Shonen Magazine in 1989, about a bullied fisherman's son who learns he can hit. He also owns a real boxing gym in Tokyo where professional fighters train. What is it called?
context: Morikawa owns JB Sports Gym, a working boxing gym in Tokyo, and he studied the sport by attending live matches at venues such as Korakuen Hall. Early in his career he briefly employed a teenage Kentaro Miura, later the creator of Berserk, as an assistant.

question: Eiichiro Oda began his pirate adventure in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1997 with its ending already planned, and One Piece has since sold more than 500 million copies worldwide. In 2006 he said how long he had first meant the story to run. How long was it?
context: Oda said in 2006 that he had first planned One Piece to last five years, with the ending already decided, and found he liked the story too much to finish it so soon. It was Japan's best-selling manga for eleven years running, 2008 to 2018.

question: Fans crowdfunded bronze statues of Eren, Mikasa and Armin as children, gazing up at a towering concrete dam that stands in for Wall Maria from Attack on Titan. The statues stand in the small mountain-ringed basin in Kyushu where Hajime Isayama grew up, and he has said many times that its scenery inspired his manga. Which town is it?
context: Isayama was born in Oyama, now part of Hita City in Oita Prefecture, and Hita made him its tourism ambassador in 2014. The statues stand in front of Oyama Dam; Isayama advised on them, and his handprint and signature sit near the base.

question: Light's black notebook in Death Note carries English writing across its cover. Takeshi Obata had first pictured a grand, Bible-like book that anyone would take for a Death Note at a glance, but he decided that design was too cumbersome. What did he draw instead?
choices: A leather-bound diary with a clasp
context: Obata first imagined the Death Notes as books a reader would automatically take for a Death Note, then switched to a more accessible college notebook. An earlier idea had the notebooks change with time and place, like scrolls in ancient Japan or the Old Testament in medieval Europe, but it was never used. The English 'Death Note' lettering on the cover became one of the manga's most iconic visual elements.

question: Edward Elric claps his hands to transmute, a faster trick than drawing a circle on the ground or having one tattooed on the palms. He came by it after the forbidden ritual that took his arm and leg, and it is uncommon among alchemists. What gave Edward the ability to skip the formal circle?
answer: He had seen the Gate of Truth and 'paid the toll' for human transmutation knowledge
choices: He had seen the Gate of Truth and 'paid the toll' for human transmutation knowledge
His father Hohenheim had secretly taught him the trick before leaving home
His mentor Izumi Curtis taught him a secret hand-clap technique she'd kept private
His prosthetic automail arm contained a built-in transmutation array invented by Winry
context: The 'paid the toll' rule is the series' central magic principle: an alchemist who has seen the Gate of Truth can transmute without drawing a circle. The hand-clap became one of the manga's most-imitated visual signatures.

question: Hirohiko Araki has spoken of where the look of JoJo's Bizarre Adventure came from. Its unreal colors came partly from the painter Paul Gauguin. Its twisting, impossible poses come from a journey he made to Italy as a young man, studying the marble figures of one sculptor. Which sculptor?
context: Araki studied Michelangelo's sculptures on a trip to Italy in his twenties, and the poses fans call JoJo-dachi grew from them. He took his strange, surreal coloring from Western painters such as Gauguin. In 2011 he drew for a Gucci exhibition in Tokyo, and in 2009 the Louvre invited him to its exhibition of comics set in the museum.

question: Yoshihiro Togashi, a lifelong fan of the occult and horror films, showed his editors rough drafts of Yu Yu Hakusho under the working title How to be a Ghost. Once the series was approved he proposed a different title, but a manga with a similar-sounding name had already begun, so he swapped in Hakusho, meaning report, the first word that came to mind. What was the title he gave up?
context: Togashi first proposed YuYu-Ki, roughly Poltergeist Chronicles, but Chin-Yu-Ki was already in print, so he chose Hakusho, Report, instead, giving YuYu Hakusho, the Poltergeist Report. His working title for the rough drafts had been How to be a Ghost.

question: Giancarlo Pasquini, an Italian musician, recorded under a stage name for Avex Trax, the Japanese label behind the Initial D soundtracks. His song 'Deja Vu' became one of the show's best-known racing tracks, the beat fans still hear when a drift car swings into a mountain bend. What was that stage name?
context: Dave Rodgers is the stage name of Giancarlo Pasquini, and 'Deja Vu' is the track of his most tied to Initial D. 'Speedy Speed Boy', another Initial D favorite, was sung by Marko Polo, an Italian singer of the same scene.

question: Trunks, a teenager from the future, travels back in Dragon Ball Z to warn the Z Fighters. In his timeline Goku has died of a heart virus and androids have killed all the Z Fighters. Trunks hands Goku something to take when the same virus strikes. What is it?
answer: A specific anti-heart-virus pharmaceutical from the future, in a Capsule Corp medicine bottle
choices: A specific anti-heart-virus pharmaceutical from the future, in a Capsule Corp medicine bottle
A sample of Dr. Gero's android-engineering blueprints in microfilm format
A Saiyan-bloodline immunity injection developed by Bulma's lab in the future
A serum from a senzu-bean cross-bred with synthetic immune-system tissue
context: The future-Trunks visit kicks off the Cell Saga; Trunks is the son of Bulma and Vegeta in a future where Goku died and the Z fighters were destroyed. Toriyama's careful work to keep both timelines coherent (the future Trunks's birth, the present-day Trunks's birth, the medicine plot point) became a model for shonen time-travel structures. Trunks's red Capsule Corp jacket and his sword (passed down from Tapion in the films) became iconic franchise looks.

question: Toshiro Hitsugaya speaks the command 'Souten ni Zase, Hyorinmaru!' in Tite Kubo's Bleach, loosely 'Reign over the frozen heavens, Hyorinmaru!', and his sealed sword turns into a long-bladed ice-dragon-themed weapon. Every Soul Reaper's sealed sword has a release phrase of its own. Hitsugaya is the captain of which squad?
context: Hitsugaya, the youngest captain in the Gotei 13, leads Squad 10, with Rangiku Matsumoto as his lieutenant. The Stealth Force, or Onmitsukido, belongs to Squad 2, whose captain Soi Fon is its commander in chief.

question: Eiichiro Oda left a 100-year gap in the history of One Piece, the Void Century, about 800 years back, when a league of kingdoms, the founders of today's World Government, wiped out a lost civilization. What is the erased kingdom called?
context: The Great Kingdom is the only name the story has given the lost civilisation, and the World Government has spent some eight hundred years suppressing its history.

question: The final chapter of Koyoharu Gotouge's Demon Slayer, in 2020, jumps about a hundred years ahead to modern Tokyo, far from the demon-fighting of the story. One boy sits reading a book and tells his sister that everyone who died fighting demons was reborn into a happier life. What is the book he is reading?
context: The modern-day epilogue fills chapter 205, the last of the manga. The boy is called Yoshiteru, and his sister is Toko. Gotouge gives the whole chapter to ordinary life in present-day Tokyo.

question: Masashi Kishimoto had lost interest in drawing manga in his early teens when a promotional image for a 1980s Japanese animated film pulled him back. He had grown up idolising the creator of Dragon Ball, but this art struck him so hard that he studied its creator's drawings and tried to imitate the style. Which film was it?
context: A promotional image for the 1988 film Akira reignited Kishimoto's passion for drawing, and he studied Katsuhiro Otomo's artwork and tried to imitate it. As a boy he had idolised Akira Toriyama, and Goku's personality helped shape Naruto.

question: Hajime Isayama told fans in interviews that he based the Survey Corps badge in Attack on Titan on a real-world military unit he had researched. The soldiers scout beyond the walls to fight giant titans, and their green uniforms carry crossed wings, one white over one blue, nicknamed the Wings of Freedom. Which real squadron did he copy?
answer: The British Royal Air Force's Pathfinder squadron of WWII
choices: The British Royal Air Force's Pathfinder squadron of WWII
The Imperial Japanese Army's Tokkotai (Special Attack Unit) of WWII
The German Luftwaffe's Schnellbomber squadron of the early Battle of Britain
The Soviet Union's Yak-9 aerial-superiority wing of the Eastern Front
context: Isayama studied multiple Western military traditions for AOT's visual design. The Survey Corps's crossed-wings emblem, the boot-and-trouser uniform style, and the cavalry-rank organization all draw from real WWII-era European militaries. The German-language naming convention for characters (Eren, Mikasa, Armin, etc.) similarly draws from Isayama's research. The Pathfinder squadron's role — finding enemy territory in the dark — fits the Survey Corps's narrative function.

question: Giorno Giovanna, fifteen years old, sets out to rise through the mafia of Naples in 2001, in Part 5 of Hirohiko Araki's JoJo's Bizarre Adventure. His fighting spirit, Gold Experience, turns stones and scraps into living plants and animals with a blow of its fists. Araki took that name from a 1995 album by an American pop star. Which musician?
context: Giorno's Stand, Gold Experience, can give life to anything its fists touch, turning lifeless objects into plants or animals. Its name matches The Gold Experience, the album Prince released in September 1995, a few months before Golden Wind began.

question: Nate River, the young albino boy his handlers call Near, plays with toys and dice on the floor in Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata's Death Note while he cracks cases. Every time he sits down to think, he does one signature nervous thing. What does Near always do while he thinks?
answer: He twists a single lock of his white hair around his index finger
choices: He twists a single lock of his white hair around his index finger
He arranges a chess match between miniature figures on a desk
He cracks his knuckles in a specific six-finger pattern
He counts dice and arranges them in pyramidal stacks on the floor
context: Near's hair-twisting habit is one of the manga's most-replicated character tics. Obata's drawings show the gesture frequently — close-ups of the finger in the curl of white hair became standard Near framing. The character is meant to be even more reclusive than L, with anxieties about social contact.

question: Studio Bones went back to Hiromu Arakawa's manga in 2009 with a second anime, Brotherhood, and stuck to it faithfully all the way to the end. The 2003 anime had run out of manga and invented its own ending, and fans complained for years. The new show's very first opening song was a fast rock number. Which act performed it?
choices: Asian Kung-Fu Generation, a rock band
context: Yui's 'Again' became one of the most-recognized anime opening themes of the late 2000s. Her solo work was characterized by acoustic guitar-driven J-rock with strong vocal melodies. The Brotherhood adaptation by Studio Bones is widely considered the better adaptation of the manga, with five different opening themes across its run. Asian Kung-Fu Generation's 'Rewrite' is iconic but belongs to the 2003 series.

question: Akira Toriyama turned Goku's hair gold for his rage-fuelled transformation against Frieza on Namek, a look shonen heroes have copied ever since. Hiroyuki Nakano, editor-in-chief of Weekly Shonen Jump, later explained on Japanese television where the gold really came from. What was Toriyama's reason?
answer: Leaving it uncolored saved the time spent inking it black
choices: Leaving it uncolored saved the time spent inking it black
Toei wanted a brighter color that would sell more toys
His editor asked for a look closer to American comic heroes
Readers had voted for a blond hero in a magazine poll

question: Hercule, a loud, muscle-bound tournament champion called Mr. Satan in the Japanese version, struts around Dragon Ball Z's Buu Saga claiming he defeated the villain Cell, when it was really the teenage hero Gohan.
